x: Rear-view mirrors are convex, not concave. Torches, headlights and shaving mirrors use concave mirrors.

s: Which one of the following is the value of 1 nanometre?
x: 1 nm = 10⁻⁹ m = 10⁻⁷ cm.

s: At 20°C, the speed of sound in water approximately
x: Sound travels at about 1480–1500 m/s in water at 20 °C (330–343 m/s in air).

s: If x the temperature of a system in Kelvin and y is the temperature of the system in °C, then the correct relation between them is
The absolute zero, i.e. temperature below which is not achievable, is about
x: Absolute zero is 0 K = −273.15 °C, i.e. about −273 °C. '−273 K' is meaningless – kelvin has no negative values.

s: The frequency (in Hz) of a note that is one octave higher than 500 Hz is
x: One octave higher means double the frequency: 2 × 500 = 1000 Hz.

s: If a body is whirled in a circle the work done on it …………
x: In circular motion the centripetal force is perpendicular to the displacement, so the work done is zero.

s: How many watts are there in metric horse power?
x: Metric horsepower = 735.5 W ≈ 736 W (the British/mechanical hp is 746 W).

s: A current I flows through a resistor. A source maintains a potential difference of V across the resistor. The energy supplied by the source in time t is
x: Energy = power × time = V × I × t.

s: Insulators have resistivity of the order of
x: NCERT gives insulators resistivities of about 10¹² to 10¹⁷ Ω m (metals 10⁻⁸–10⁻⁶).

s: ........ states that the total current entering a junction is equal to the total current leaving the junction.
x: Kirchhoff's first (junction) law: total current entering a junction equals the total current leaving it (conservation of charge).

s: .......... .is not related to gases.
x: Boyle's, Avogadro's and Charles's laws are gas laws; Joule's law (H = I²Rt) concerns heating by electric current.

s: How much calories are there in a Joule?
x: 1 cal = 4.186 J, so 1 J ≈ 0.24 cal.

s: The motion of a freely falling body is an example of ........... accelerated motion.
x: A freely falling body has a constant acceleration g, so its motion is uniformly accelerated.

s: Why does a cannon recoil after firing?
x: Firing pushes the shell forward and the cannon back by an equal and opposite reaction – Newton's third law (equivalently, momentum conservation).

s: A body is acted upon by two unequal forces in opposite directions, but not in one line. The effect is that the body will have
o: neither the rotational nor the translational motion.
rotational as well as translational motion.
x: Two unequal opposite forces not in one line give a net force (translation) and a torque (rotation), so both motions result.

s: Boiling point of water is .... .
x: Water boils at 100 °C = 212 °F at standard pressure.

s: The absolute zero temperature is 0°K. In °C unit, which one of the following is the absolute zero temperature?
Which finger shows the direction of current in Fleming’s left hand rule?
x: In Fleming's left-hand rule the forefinger shows the field, the middle finger the current and the thumb the force (motion).

s: The heat produced by current in wire during time t is determined by ……… .
x: Joule's law of heating: H = I²Rt.

s: As the object covers unequal distances in equal intervals of time, it is said to be in ......... motion.
x: Unequal distances in equal intervals of time = non-uniform motion.

s: The sensation of sound persists in the human brain for about
x: The sensation of a sound persists in the brain for about 0.1 s – why an echo needs a 0.1 s delay (17.2 m distance).

s: More density of the particles in the medium through which sound travels, creates more ……… and vice versa.
x: Where particles are crowded (compressions) the density and pressure are high; rarefactions have low pressure.

s: If an object is at rest, then the time (X-axis) versus distance (Y-axis) graph
x: At rest the distance does not change with time, so the distance–time graph is a horizontal line parallel to the time axis.

s: The angle in which a cricket ball should be hit to travel maximum horizontal distance is
x: Range R = u² sin2θ / g is maximum when sin2θ = 1, i.e. θ = 45°.

s: Magnetic meridian is an imaginary
x: The magnetic meridian is the vertical plane through the magnetic axis of a freely suspended magnet (the magnetic N–S direction).

s:
Statement I A compass needle placed near a current-carrying wire will get deflected. Statement II A current-carrying wire creates magnetic field around it.
Codes
o: Statement I and statement II are correct and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I
Statement I and statement II are correct, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I
Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is correct
x: A current-carrying wire produces a magnetic field around it, which is why a nearby compass needle deflects – II explains I.

s: Two identical solid pieces, one of gold and other of silver, when immersed completely in water exhibit equal weights. When weighed in air (given that, density of gold is greater than that of silver),
o: the gold piece will weigh more.
the silver piece will weigh more.
Both silver and gold pieces weigh equal.
weighing will depend on their masses.
x: Apparent weight in water = W(1 − ρw/ρ). Equal apparent weights mean the less dense silver loses a bigger share, so its true (air) weight is larger.

s: A person is standing on a frictionless horizontal ground. How can he move by a certain distance on this ground?
x: On frictionless ground he cannot push the ground backward; expelling air by sneezing (or throwing anything) gives him an opposite push – momentum conservation.

s: When the direction of motion of coil is perpendicular to the electromagnetic field, then the value of induced current is ……… .
x: Induced current is maximum when the coil moves perpendicular to the magnetic field (maximum rate of flux cutting) and zero when it moves parallel.

s:
A spring can be used to determine the mass m of an object in two ways : I by measuring the extension in the spring due to the object and II by measuring the oscillation period for the given mass.
Which of these methods can be used in a space-station orbiting the earth?
x: In orbit everything is in free fall (weightless), so the object stretches the spring by nothing; the oscillation period T = 2π√(m/k) does not depend on g and still works.

s: When temperature difference between liquid and its surroundings is doubled, the rate of loss of heat will
x: Newton's law of cooling: rate of heat loss ∝ temperature difference, so doubling the difference doubles the rate.

s: Which one of the following force is non-central and non-conservative?
x: Friction acts against motion along the surface, not along a line joining centres (non-central), and its work depends on path (non-conservative). Electric and gravitational forces are central and conservative.

s: If a physical quantity has the units- ampere meters per second squared, then what are it’s dimensions?
x: Ampere → [I], metre → [L], per second squared → [T⁻²]: the dimensions are [I L T⁻²].

s: A rectangular coil of copper wire is rotating in a magnetic field. The direction of the induced current changes once in each?
x: In a coil rotating in a magnetic field the induced current reverses direction once every half revolution, giving alternating current.

s: Ability to distinguish two closely placed objects is
x: Resolving power is an instrument's ability to show two close objects as separate. Magnifying power only enlarges the image; 'video' and 'distinguish' power are not terms.

s: Which of these travels in glass with minimum velocity?
x: Violet has the highest refractive index in glass, so it travels slowest (v = c/n). Red light is the fastest of the colours in glass.

s: Which of the following is not a unit of speed?
x: Speed is distance per time, so m/s, km/h and cm/s are speed units. m²/h is area per time, not speed.

s: For a body moving with uniform acceleration its final velocity equals ........... .
x: With uniform acceleration the average velocity is (u + v)/2, so v = 2 × average velocity − u. The other combinations do not follow from this relation.

s: The first equation of motion gives the relation between
x: The first equation v = u + at links velocity and time. The second (s = ut + ½at²) links position and time, the third links position and velocity.

s: The second equation of motion gives the relation between
x: The second equation s = ut + ½at² gives position (displacement) against time. Velocity–time is the first equation and position–velocity the third.

s: The rate of change of displacement with time is called as ...... .
x: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, and force is not a rate of displacement.

s: In a vacuum, a five-rupee coin a, feather of sparrow bird and a mango are dropped simultaneously from the same height. The time taken by them to reach the bottom is t1, t 2 and t 3 , respectively. In this situation, we will observe that
x: With no air resistance every body falls with the same acceleration g, so all three take the same time (t1 = t2 = t3). Mass does not affect free-fall time.

s: At magnetic poles, the angle of dip is
x: At the magnetic poles the needle stands vertical, so dip is 90°. Dip is zero at the magnetic equator.

s: The temperature which has the same reading on both Fahrenheit and Celsius scales is
x: Setting F = C in F = 9C/5 + 32 gives C = −40. So −40 °C = −40 °F.

s: A man weighing 70 kg is coming down in lift. It the cable of the lift breaks sudden, the weight of the man would become
x: If the cable breaks, man and lift fall freely with g, so the floor pushes on him with no force and his apparent weight becomes zero.

s: The unit of pressure is
o: None of the above/More than one of the above
x:
Printed BPSC key: None of the above. Most books treat kg/cm² (as kgf/cm²) as a pressure unit, which would make (a) correct.
The printed BPSC 2019 key is 'None of the above/More than one of the above': kg/cm² is mass per unit area; the pressure unit is kgf/cm² (or the SI pascal, N/m²).

s: Pressure is a scalar quantity because
o: it is the ratio of force to area and both force and area are vectors.
it is the ratio of magnitude of force to area.
it is the ratio of component of force (normal to area) to area
x: Pressure is the normal component of force divided by area; it acts equally in all directions and has no direction of its own, so it is scalar.

s: One nanometer is equal to ……… meters.
x: One nanometre is 10⁻⁹ m. 10⁻⁶ is micro and 10⁻¹² is pico.

s: Magnetic keepers are used to protect magnets from
x: Soft-iron keepers close the magnetic circuit across the poles, which stops the magnet's own demagnetising field from weakening it. They do not shield heating or outside fields.

s: Ice is packed in saw dust because
o: saw dust will not get melted easily.
saw dust is poor conductor of heat.
saw dust is a good conductor of heat.
saw dust does not stick to the ice.
x: Sawdust is a poor conductor of heat (air trapped in it), so heat reaches the ice slowly. It is not a good conductor.

s: According to the Second Law of Motion, for a given force, acceleration is inversely proportional to the ……… of an object.
x: From F = ma, for a fixed force the acceleration is inversely proportional to the mass. Density and volume do not enter the law.

s: Acceleration due to gravity of planet decreases with ..... .
o: decrease in radius of the planet
increase in mass of the planet
decrease in mass of the body
increase in altitude from surface of the planet
x: g falls with altitude because distance from the centre grows. Smaller radius or larger planet mass would increase g, and the falling body's mass does not matter.

s: A liquid disturbed by stirring comes to rest due to
x: Viscosity, the internal friction between liquid layers, damps the motion of a stirred liquid. Surface tension acts only at the surface.

s: The density of water is 1 g./cc. This is strictly valid at
x: Water reaches its maximum density of 1 g/cc at 4 °C; between 4 °C and 0 °C it expands. So the value is strictly valid at 4 °C.

s: Rocket works on the principle of
x: Hot gases pushed backward (action) push the rocket forward (reaction): Newton's third law, equivalent to momentum conservation. There is no Newton's fourth law.

s: Which of the following statements regarding magnetic field is not correct?
o: Magnetic field is a quantity that has direction and magnitude.
magnetic field lines are closed curves.
Magnetic field lines are open curves.
No two magnetic field lines are found to cross each other.
x: Magnetic field lines are always closed loops, so 'open curves' is the incorrect statement. The field is a vector, and lines never cross.

s: Which one of the following is not a luminous object?
x: The Moon shines only by reflected sunlight, so it is non-luminous. The Sun, an electric lamp and a candle make their own light.

s: A positively charged particle projected towards West is deflected towards North by a magnetic field. What is the direction of magnetic field?
x: For a positive charge F = q(v × B); with v to the west and F to the north, B must point vertically upward (Fleming's left-hand rule).

s: What is the term of the space around a magnet where its influence can be detected?
x: The space around a magnet where its influence is felt is the magnetic field. Electrostatic and gravitational fields come from charges and masses.

s: The centre of the reflecting surface of a spherical mirror is called the
x: The pole is the centre of a mirror's reflecting surface. The centre of curvature is the centre of the sphere it belongs to, and the focus is halfway to it.

s: The spring constant of a spring depends on its
o: thickness, its diameter and its material
x: The stiffness k depends on the material (rigidity), wire thickness and coil diameter; length alone or material alone is incomplete.

s: Which one of the following statement about magnetic field lines is not correct?
o: They can emanate from a point.
They do not cross each other.
Field lines between two poles cannot be precisely straight lines at the ends.
There are no field lines within a bar magnet.
x:
Keys differ: Testbook keys 'They can emanate from a point'; Examrobot keys 'There are no field lines within a bar magnet'. Strictly both (a) and (d) are false; (c) is true.
Magnetic field lines are closed loops and there are no magnetic monopoles, so they cannot emanate from a point. Option (c) is a true statement (lines near the pole ends are curved), so the printed key was wrong; (d) is also false (lines run S → N inside the magnet).

s: When an object is kept between two parallel plane mirrors then what is the number of images formed?
x: Between parallel mirrors light reflects back and forth endlessly, giving infinitely many images (n = 360/θ − 1 with θ = 0).

s: During ............. motion of an object along a straight line, the change in velocity of the object for any time interval is zero.
x: In uniform motion along a straight line velocity does not change, so the change in velocity over any interval is zero.

s: If the distance-time graph is a curve then it represents ........... .
x: A curved distance–time graph means the slope (speed) keeps changing, i.e. non-uniform speed. A straight line would mean uniform speed.

s: The apparent weight of man in a lift is less the real weight when
o: the lift is going up with an acceleration.
the lift is going down with uniform speed.
the lift is going up with uniform speed.
the lift is going down with an acceleration.
x: Apparent weight is m(g − a) when the lift accelerates downward, so it is less. At uniform speed (up or down) apparent weight equals real weight.

s: The moment of inertia of a body does not depend upon its
x: Moment of inertia I = Σmr² depends on mass, its distribution and the axis of rotation. Angular velocity does not change it.

s: A solid disc and a solid sphere have the same mass and same radius. Which one has the higher moment of inertia about its centre of mass?
o: Both have the same moment of inertia.
The information provided is not sufficient to answer the question.
x: A solid disc has I = ½MR² = 0.5MR², a solid sphere 2/5 MR² = 0.4MR². So the disc's moment of inertia is higher.

s: The period of a simple pendulum is doubled, when
o: the Mass of the bob is doubled.
its length is made four times.
The Mass of the bob and the length of the pendulum are doubled.
x: T = 2π√(L/g), so T ∝ √L; making the length four times doubles T. Mass of the bob does not affect the period.

s: Which one of the following is not a contact force?
x: Gravity acts at a distance without contact. Push, friction and strain (tension) need contact.

s: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion. Which one of the following statements about the acceleration of the oscillating particle is true?
o: It is always in the opposite direction to velocity.
It is proportional to the frequency of oscillation.
It is minimum when the speed is maximum.
It decreases as the potential energy increases.
x: In SHM a = −ω²x, so acceleration is zero at the mean position, where speed is maximum. It is proportional to ω² (not frequency) and grows as potential energy grows.

s: When the milk is churned vigorously the cream from it is separated out due to
x: On churning, the denser milk is thrown outward and the lighter cream collects at the centre, explained by centrifugal force (as in a cream separator).

s: A brick is thrown vertically from an aircraft flying 2 km above the earth. The brick will fall with a
o: constant speed for some time then with constant acceleration as it means the earth.
x: Neglecting air resistance, the brick falls with constant acceleration g. Its speed and velocity keep increasing, so they are not constant.

s: The distance-time graph for the motion of an object moving with a constant speed is a
x: For constant speed the distance–time graph is a straight line (constant slope). A curve shows changing speed.

s: If the distance between the earth and the sun were twice what it is now, the gravitational force exerted on the earth by the sun would be
o: twice as large as it is now.
four times as large as it is now.
one-fourth of what it is now.
Half of what it is now.
x: By Newton's law F ∝ 1/r², so doubling the distance cuts the force to 1/4. It is not halved.

s: In which of the following places is the acceleration due to gravity zero?
o: At the centre of the earth
x: At the centre the Earth's mass pulls equally in all directions, so g is zero. g is maximum at the poles and slightly less at the equator.

s: To change a temperature from the Kelvin scale to the Celsius scale, you have to
x: T(°C) = T(K) − 273, so you subtract 273. Adding 273 converts Celsius to Kelvin.

s: Due to atmospheric refraction, sunrise in advanced and sunset is delayed by about
x: NCERT: atmospheric refraction makes the Sun visible about 2 minutes before actual sunrise and about 2 minutes after actual sunset.

s: A bomb explodes on the moon. You will heard its sound on earth after ………
o: you cannot hear the sound of explosion
x: Sound needs a material medium; space between the Moon and Earth is a vacuum, so the explosion cannot be heard on Earth.

s: To open a door easily, the handle should be fixed
o: away from mid-point opposite to hinges
x: Torque = force × perpendicular distance from the axis, so a handle far from the hinges opens the door with least force.

s: What is the direction of magnetic field lines in a magnet?
x: Outside the magnet the field lines run from the north pole to the south pole (inside they go S → N, forming closed loops). East/west are not magnetic poles.

s: Which of the following statements is true? The velocity of sound is
o: less in summer than in winter.
more in summer than in winter.
x: Sound travels faster in warmer air, so its velocity is higher in summer than in winter. It does depend on temperature.

s: In a periscope, the two plane mirrors are kept
o: at an angle of 60° with each other.
at an angle of 45° with each other.
x: The two periscope mirrors are parallel to each other, each inclined at 45° to the tube's axis. They are not at 45° to each other.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct about the magnification of an optical microscope?
o: Magnification increases with the increase in focal length of eyepiece.
Magnification increases with the increase in focal length of objective.
Magnification does not depend upon the focal length of eyepiece.
Magnification decreases with the increase in focal length of eyepiece.
x: Magnification of a compound microscope is inversely proportional to the focal lengths of objective and eyepiece, so it decreases as the eyepiece focal length increases.

s: The working principle of a mercury thermometer is
o: change in density of matter on heating.
change in mass of matter on heating.
x: The mercury column rises because mercury expands on heating. Mass does not change, and the scale reads temperature.

s:
Which of the following angles are equal in case of plane mirror?

I. Angle of incidence

II. Angle of refraction

III. Angle of reflection
o: All the given angles are equal
x: At a plane mirror the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection. Refraction is bending into another medium and does not apply here.

s: The SI unit for the average velocity is ……… .
x: Velocity (average or instantaneous) is measured in m/s in SI. km/s is not the SI base form and m/s² is acceleration.

s: Light waves are ……… .
x: Light is an electromagnetic wave with oscillating electric and magnetic fields. It is neither purely electric nor purely magnetic.

s: Which of the following quantities does not have any unit?
x: Relative density is the ratio of a substance's density to that of water, so it has no unit. Speed, density and acceleration all have units.

s: Electromagnet is constructed with which of the following?
x: Soft iron magnetises strongly when current flows and loses magnetism when it stops, so it is used in electromagnets. Steel retains magnetism and suits permanent magnets.

s:
Which of the following statements are correct?

I. Change in magnetic field produces induced current.

II. Flow of current in a conductor produces magnetic field.

III. Magnetic field related to coil can be produced by motion between conductor and coil.
x: All three statements describe electromagnetism: a changing field or relative motion between magnet/conductor and coil induces current, and current produces a magnetic field.

s: A metal plate with a circular hole at the centre is heated. What will happen to the area of the hole?
o: Will increase first and then decrease
x: On heating, every linear dimension of the plate grows, including the hole's diameter, so the hole's area increases.

s: Integrated circuits are made up of which of the following?
x: ICs are fabricated on silicon wafers, the main semiconductor. Aluminium is only used for interconnects; glass and iron are not the base.

s: Which one of the following is not a semiconductor?
x: Quartz (SiO2) is an insulator. Silicon, germanium and gallium arsenide are semiconductors.

s: When a piece of pure silicon is doped with aluminium, then
o: the conductivity of the doped silicon piece will remain the same.
the doped silicon piece will become n-type.
the doped silicon piece will become p-type.
the resistivity of the doped silicon piece will increase.
x: Aluminium has three valence electrons, creating holes, so Si becomes p-type and conducts better. Pentavalent dopants would make it n-type.

s: If there were no gravity, which of the following will not be there for a fluid?
x: Upthrust arises from the pressure difference due to the weight of fluid, which needs gravity. Viscosity and surface tension are intermolecular and would remain.

s: Soap bubble attains spherical shape due to ……… .
x: Surface tension minimises surface area, and a sphere has the least area for a volume, so bubbles are spherical.

s: Which one of the following statement(s) is/are not correct?
o: The response of the ear to sound of increasing intensity is approximately logarithmic.
The sensitivity of the human ear does not vary with the frequency of the sound.
When two or more waves traverse the same medium, the displacement of any element of the medium is the algebraic sum of the displacements due to each wave.
Longitudinal waves can travel in all media; solids, liquids and gases.
x: The ear is not equally sensitive at all frequencies (most sensitive about 1–4 kHz), so statement (b) is wrong. The other three are correct physics.

s: Action and reaction …..… .
x: Action and reaction are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction, acting on two different bodies. They are never on the same body or in the same direction.

s:
A brass ball is tied to a thin wire and swung so as to move uniformly in a horizontal circle.
Which of the following statements in this regard is/are ture?

I. The ball moves with constant velocity.

II. The ball moves with constant speed.

III. The ball moves with constant acceleration.

IV. The magnitude of the acceleration of the ball is constant.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
x: In uniform circular motion speed and the magnitude of centripetal acceleration stay constant, but their directions keep changing, so velocity and acceleration (as vectors) are not constant.

s: Which one of the following statements about sound is not correct?
o: Sound travels at a speed slower than the speed of light.
Sound travels faster in moist air than in dry air.
x: Sound waves in air are longitudinal, not transverse, so (b) is wrong. Sound is slower than light and faster in moist air.

s: In simple harmonic motion, acceleration is at
x: In SHM a = −ω²x, so the acceleration is maximum at the amplitude (extreme) and zero at equilibrium; it is not constant.

s: Quality of a musical note depends on
o: velocity of sound in the medium.
x: Quality (timbre) depends on the harmonics present, i.e. the waveform. Pitch depends on fundamental frequency and loudness on amplitude.

s:
Consider the following statement. If there were no phenomenon of capillarity, then

I. It would be difficult to use a kerosene lamp.

II. One would not be able to use a straw to consume a soft drink.

III. The blotting paper would fail to function.

IV. The big trees that we see around would not have grown on the earth.
Which of the following statements given above are correct?
o: I, II, III and IV only
x: A kerosene wick, blotting paper and water rise in tall trees rely on capillarity (UPSC key I, III, IV). Drinking through a straw works by atmospheric pressure.

s: Waves produced at the bottom of the sea due to an explosion are… .
x: Fluids cannot support shear, so only longitudinal (compression) waves travel through sea water. Transverse waves need a solid.

s:
Which of the following are the characteristics of electromagnetic waves?

I. They are elastic waves.

II. They can also move in vacuum.

III. They have electric and magnetic components which are mutually perpendicular.

IV. They move with a speed equal to 3 lakh meters per second.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: EM waves cross vacuum and have mutually perpendicular electric and magnetic fields (II, III). They are not elastic waves, and their speed is 3 lakh km/s, not 3 lakh m/s.

s:
Which of the following occurs due to refraction?

I. The apparent displacement of a pencil, partly immersed in water.

II. Sun appears before the sunrise.

III. Sky appears blue.
x: The bent-looking pencil and the Sun seen before sunrise are due to refraction. The blue sky is due to scattering of light.

s:
In case of a compound microscope, which of the following statements is/are correct?

I. The focal length of the eyepiece is larger than the focal length of the objective.

II. The focal length of the eyepiece is smaller than the focal length of the objective.

III. The image produced in a normal optical microscope is real.

IV. The image produced in a normal optical microscope is virtual.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
x: The objective has a very short focal length and the eyepiece a longer one; the final image seen is virtual (I and IV).

s:
Which of the following are the properties of an electron?

I. Electron is a constituent of cathode ray.

II. Electron is a negatively charged particle.

III. The mass of the electron is equal to the mass of the proton.

IV. Electron is deflected by the electric field but not by magnetic field.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Electrons make up cathode rays and are negatively charged (I, II). Their mass is about 1/1836 of a proton's, and they are deflected by magnetic fields too.

s: An object is placed in front of a concave mirror at a point between its centre of curvature and focus. The image will be formed at
o: a point beyond the centre of curvature.
a point between the focus and the centre of curvature.
x: For an object between C and F a concave mirror forms a real, inverted, magnified image beyond C.

s:
Which of the following statement(s) about specific heat of a body is/are correct?

I. It depends upon mass and shape of the body.

II. It is independent of mass and shape of the body.

III. It depends only upon the temperature of the body.
x: Specific heat is per unit mass, so it does not depend on the body's mass or shape (II). It depends on the material, not only on temperature, so III is wrong.

s:
Which type of image is always formed by a convex mirror?

I. Real
II. Virtual

III. Enlarged
x: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image. It is never real or enlarged.

s:
Which of the following statement(s) about electromagnetic waves, sound waves and water waves is/are correct?

I. They exhibit reflection.

II. They carry energy.

III. They exert pressure.

IV. They can travel in vacuum.
x: All three kinds of wave show reflection, carry energy and exert pressure. Only EM waves travel in vacuum, so IV is false.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct? The velocity of sound
o: does not depend upon the nature of media.
is maximum in gases and minimum in liquids.
is maximum in solids and minimum in liquids.
is maximum in solids and minimum in gases.
x: Sound is fastest in solids and slowest in gases, liquids being in between. It depends on the medium.

s: A boat full of iron nails is floating on water in a lake. When the iron nails are removed, the water level
x: A floating boat displaces water equal to its total weight; taking the nails out lightens it, so it displaces less water and the level falls.

s: The term LASER stand for
o: Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation
Light Amplification by Spontaneous Emission of Radiation
Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Rays
Light Amplification by Stimulated Energy of Radiation
x: LASER stands for Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation. Spontaneous emission does not produce laser light.

s: When pure water boils vigorously, the bubbles that rise to the surface are composed primarily of
x: Boiling forms bubbles of water vapour inside the liquid. Dissolved air is expelled early; water does not decompose into hydrogen and oxygen.

s: A balloon filled with helium rises in air because
o: air exerts an upward force on the balloon
helium is less dense than air.
helium pushes down on the air below the balloon.
x: Helium is far less dense than air, so the upthrust of displaced air exceeds the balloon's weight. The balloon is not weightless.

s: Which one of the following is not an electromagnetic wave?
x: Sound is a mechanical, longitudinal wave needing a medium. Light, radio waves and microwaves are electromagnetic.

s: Which one of the following has the longest wavelength?
x: Infrared has longer wavelength than visible light, UV and gamma rays, so it is the longest of the four.

s: A car starts from Bengaluru, goes 50 km in a straight line towards South, immediately turns around and returns to Bengaluru. The time taken for this round trip is 2h. The magnitude of the average velocity of the car for this round trip
o: cannot be calculated without knowing acceleration
x: Returning to the start makes displacement zero, so average velocity is zero. The average speed would be 50 km/h.

s: It is easy to burst a gas-filled balloon with a needle than with a nail. It is because
o: nail is more longer than needle.
nail exerts more pressure than needle on the balloon.
needle exerts more pressure than nail on the balloon.
gas is reactive with the needle.
x: The needle tip has a much smaller area, so the same force gives greater pressure (P = F/A) and bursts the balloon easily.

s: The quality or tone of a musical sound produced by a stringed instrument depends on
o: length of the strings in the instrument.
x: The quality or timbre of a sound depends on its waveform (the harmonics mixed with the fundamental). Frequency decides pitch and amplitude loudness.

s: Which of the following is the methods of heat transfer?
x: The three modes of heat transfer are conduction, convection and radiation. Evaporation, revolution and thermal expansion are not modes of transfer.

s: A thermometer is used to measure
x: A thermometer measures temperature (degree of hotness), not the quantity of heat.

s: ……… is not an example of refraction of light.
o: Bending of light while passing through a medium
x: Lateral inversion is caused by reflection in a plane mirror. Twinkling of stars, mirages and bending of light are all refraction effects.

s: Which of the following quantities have its SI unit named after Blaise Pascal?
x: The pascal (N/m²), named after Blaise Pascal, is the SI unit of pressure. Energy and work use the joule and power the watt.

s: A deep sea diver may hurt his ear drum during diving because of
x: Water pressure grows with depth (P = hρg), and this high pressure can damage the eardrum. Atmospheric pressure is small in comparison.

s: Two cars, passing each other at high speed, are in danger of side swiping because
o: of the increase in air pressure in the space between them.
of decrease in the velocity of air molecules between them.
of decrease in air pressure in the space between them.
of the increase in the velocity of air molecules between them.
x: Air speeds up between the cars, so pressure there falls (Bernoulli); the higher outside pressure pushes the cars together.

s: The SI unit of weight is
x: Weight is a force, so its SI unit is the newton. kg and g are units of mass; dyne is the CGS unit of force.

s: Water is used in a hot water bag because
x: Water's high specific heat lets it store a lot of heat and release it slowly. Specific gravity has nothing to do with it.

s: A liquid is kept in a glass beaker. Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the pressure exerted by the liquid column at the base of the beaker?
o: The pressure depends on the area of the base of the beaker.
The pressure depends on the height of liquid column.
The pressure does not depend on the density of the liquid.
The pressure neither depends on the area of the base of the beaker nor on the height of liquid column.
x: Pressure at the base is hρg, so it depends on the height of the column (and density), not on the area of the base.

s: If ice floating on water in a vessel melts, the water level in the vessel …… .
x: Floating ice displaces water equal to its own weight; on melting it turns into exactly that volume of water, so the level stays the same.

s: When water freezes its density
x: Water expands about 9% on freezing, so its density decreases; that is why ice floats.

s: During the melting of solid, its temperature
o: may increase or decrease depending on the nature of solid.
x: While a solid melts the heat supplied is used as latent heat to change state, so temperature stays constant until melting is complete.

s: If the speed of a moving magnet inside a coil increases, the electric current in the coil
x: Induced emf is proportional to the rate of change of flux, so moving the magnet faster increases the current.

s: How is the kinetic energy of a moving object affected if the net work done on it is positive?
x: By the work–energy theorem, net work equals the change in kinetic energy, so positive net work increases KE.

s: The surface tension of water on adding detergent to it
x: Detergents are surfactants that lower the surface tension of water, which helps it wet and clean. It does not become zero.

s: Which one of the following is not a result of surface tension?
o: Removal of dirt by soap or detergent
x: Spherical raindrops, capillary rise and removal of dirt by detergents (lowered surface tension) are surface-tension effects. Flow of a liquid is governed by viscosity and pressure.

s: The slope of a distance-time graph shows .............. .
x: The slope of a distance-time graph is distance/time, which is speed.

s: The tendency of undisturbed objects to stay at rest or to keep moving with the same velocity is called
x: Inertia is the tendency of a body to stay at rest or in uniform motion (Newton's first law).

s: Which of the following quantity is a measure of inertia?
x: Mass measures inertia; weight depends on gravity.

s: The rate of change of momentum of a body is equal to the resultant
x: By Newton's second law, force = rate of change of momentum.

s: The Second Law of Motion states that
o: Every object will move in a uniform motion when a net force is applied.
The rate of change of momentum of an object is proportional to the net force applied on the object in the direction of net force.
Every object will remain at rest or in a state of uniform motion unless compelled to change its state by the action of a net force.
The rate of change of speed of a body will change with the net force applied.
x: Newton's second law says the rate of change of momentum is proportional to the net applied force, in the direction of the force. Option 3 is the first law.

s:
Statement I: When a gun is fired, it pushes back with much less velocity than the velocity of the bullet.
Statement II: Velocity of the recoiling gun is less because the gun is much heavier than the bullet.
Codes
o: Both the statements are individually true and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I
Both the statements are individually true but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I
Statement I is true, but statement II is false
Statement I is false, but statement II is true
x: Momentum is conserved, so the gun and bullet get equal and opposite momenta; the gun is far heavier, so its recoil velocity is much smaller. Statement II therefore correctly explains Statement I.

s: Which of the following physical quantity measures the rate of work done?
x: Power is the rate of doing work (work/time).

s: For a missile launched with a velocity less than the earth’s escape velocity, the total energy is
x: A body with speed below escape velocity is gravitationally bound, so its total energy (KE + PE) is negative.

s: The spring balance works on the principle of …… .
x: A spring balance works on Hooke's law: extension is proportional to the applied force.

s: 1 pascal equal 1 ……… .
x: Pascal is the unit of pressure, defined as force per area, so 1 Pa = 1 N m⁻².

s: According to ………, pressure is equal to the force divided by the area on which it acts.
x:
Official key / most books: Pascal's law. Strictly: P = F/A is the definition of pressure; Pascal's law is about transmission of pressure in a confined fluid (PMF General Science Part 6 p.36).
Pressure as force per unit area is the quantity whose unit and fluid law carry Pascal's name, so Pascal's law is the intended answer; Hooke's law is about elasticity, Stefan-Boltzmann about radiation and Newton's laws about motion.

s: The pressure of a fluid varies with depth h as p = p0 + ρgh, where ρ is the fluid density. This expression is associated with
x:
Official key / most books: Pascal's law. Strictly: p = p0 + ρgh is the hydrostatic pressure equation (PMF General Science Part 6 p.35); Pascal's law proper is the equal transmission of pressure (p.36).
p = p0 + ρgh is the hydrostatic pressure relation, which books treat under Pascal's law of fluid pressure. Bernoulli's principle relates pressure and speed of flow, and Archimedes' principle is about buoyancy.

s: Which of the following physicists explained the existence of Buoyant force?
x: Archimedes' principle explains buoyancy, so Archimedes explained the buoyant force.

s: Which law/principle states that when a body is immersed fully or partially in a fluid, it experiences an upward force that is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it?
x: The upward force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced is Archimedes' principle (buoyancy).

s: Purity of a metal can be determined with the help of
x: Archimedes' principle relates to buoyancy and the density of the body, and density helps check a metal's purity.

s: Decibel is the unit of
x: The decibel is the unit of sound level (intensity of sound). It is not a unit of the speed of light, heat or mass.

s: Which one of the following frequency range is sensitive to human ears?
x: The audible range for humans is 20 Hz to 20 kHz, i.e. 20-20000 Hz.

s: The frequency of ultrasonic waves is
x: Ultrasound is sound above 20 kHz, the upper limit of human hearing.

s: What is called the sound wave above than frequencies of 30,000 Hz?
x: Sound above 20 kHz is ultrasound, so a wave above 30,000 Hz is ultrasound; infrasound is below 20 Hz.

s: In which of the following mirror size of image formed is always equal to the size of object?
x: A plane mirror always forms an image the same size as the object, whereas convex and concave mirrors change the size depending on object position.

s: Which one of the following is not true about the image formed by a plane mirror?
o: It is of the same size as the subject.
It is formed as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.
x: A plane mirror forms a virtual image, not a real one, so the statement that it is real is false; the other statements are true.

s: Which one of the following statement is correct for a plane mirror?
o: The size of the image of an object placed in front of the mirror is slightly less than that of the object.
The image is virtual, erect and laterally inverted.
x: A plane mirror gives a virtual, erect, laterally inverted image of the same size; its focal length is infinite, so the other options are wrong.

s: A curved mirror where the reflecting surface is curved inwards is called a
x: A concave mirror has its reflecting surface curved inwards (like the inside of a sphere); a convex mirror bulges outwards.

s: In which mirror, image formed is virtual, correct and point sized?
x: A convex mirror always forms a virtual, erect, diminished image (point-sized for a very distant object); plane and concave mirrors do not do this for all positions.

s: If you look into a mirror and find that the image your reflexion is smaller than you, then the type of the mirror is
x: A convex mirror gives a diminished image (magnification less than 1), so the image looks smaller.

s: What is the Centre of Curvature of a spherical mirror?
o: It is a point from which the rays of light appear to be coming from on the principal axis a convex mirror.
It is the centre of a hollow sphere of which the spherical mirror is a part.
It is the midpoint of spherical mirror.
It is the point of the principal axis through which rays of light parallel to the principal axis pass after reflection.
x: The centre of curvature is the centre of the hollow sphere of which the mirror is a part.

s: Name the type of mirror used in the headlight of vehicles.
x: A vehicle headlight uses a concave mirror; a convex mirror is used as the rear-view mirror.

s: The mirror used by a dentist to examine the teeth of patients is
x: A dentist uses a concave mirror because with the object within the focus it gives an erect, magnified virtual image of the teeth.

s: Convex mirrors are used as a rear view mirror in motion cycles because
o: it forms smaller image as compared with object.
x: A convex mirror forms a virtual, erect, diminished image (magnification less than 1) and gives a wider field of view, so all the reasons given are true.

s: If objects appear enlarged and inverted in a rear view mirror, then which type of mirror is used?
x: A concave mirror can give an enlarged image and an inverted real image; a convex mirror always gives a diminished erect image, and a plane mirror gives a same-size image.

s: Concave mirror is used in headlights of vehicles, because it
o: focuses light from the bulb onto nearby vehicles.
fits well into the shape of the headlight.
x: The bulb sits at the focus of the concave mirror, so reflected light goes out as a parallel beam.

s: The outside rear view mirror of modern automobiles is marked with warning ‘objects in mirror are closer than they appear’. Such mirrors are
o: concave mirrors with very large focal lengths.
concave mirrors with very small focal lengths.
x: The rear-view mirror is convex, and its magnification below 1 makes objects look smaller and farther than they are.

s: In a concave mirror if object is placed at centre of curvature then image will be ……… .
x: When an object is at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror, the image forms at the centre of curvature, real, inverted and the same size.

s: What will be the size of image formed by a concave mirror when an object placed between pole and focus?
x: For an object between the pole and focus of a concave mirror, the image is virtual, erect and enlarged.

s: Find the position of the image formed by a concave mirror when the object is placed between P and F?
x: For an object between P and F of a concave mirror, the reflected rays diverge, so the virtual image forms behind the mirror.

s: In case of a concave mirror, if an object is kept between principal focus F and pole P of the mirror, then which one of the following statements about the image is not correct?
o: The image will be enlarged or magnified.
The image will be formed at infinity.
x: For an object between F and P of a concave mirror, the image is virtual, erect and magnified, and it is formed behind the mirror. It is not formed at infinity (that happens when the object is at F), so option 3 is not correct.

s: An object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror of focal length 16 cm. If the object is shifted by 8 cm towards the focus, then the nature of the image would be
x: The centre of curvature is at 32 cm (R = 2f). Moving the object 8 cm toward the focus puts it at 24 cm, which is between F (16 cm) and C (32 cm). The image is then real, inverted and magnified, beyond C.

s: In a magnifying glass ……… lens is used.
x: A magnifying glass is a convex lens. An object within its focal length gives a virtual, erect, magnified image.

s: When a convex lens produces a real image of an object, the minimum distance between the object and image is equal to
o: the focal length of the convex lens.
twice the focal length of the convex lens.
four times the focal length of the convex lens.
one-half of the focal length of the convex lens.
x: For a real image from a convex lens, the object-image distance is u + v. Its minimum is 4f, reached when the object is at 2f and the image is at 2f.

s:
A lens has a power of +2.0 Dioptre.
Which one of the following statements about the lens is true?
o: The lens is concave and has a focal length of 0.5 m.
The lens is convex and has a focal length of 2.0 m.
The lens is convex and has a focal length of 0.5 m.
The lens is concave and has a focal length of 2.0 m.
x: Power P = 1/f, so f = 1/2 = 0.5 m. Positive power means a convex (converging) lens, so 'convex, 0.5 m' is right; 2.0 m confuses P with f.

s: The light energy escaping from the sun can be spread by
o: a combination of a convex lens and a concave lens.
x: Rain drops spread sunlight into its colours by refraction and dispersion, as in a rainbow. A plane mirror or lens alone does not do this.

s: In long-sightedness, images are formed
x: In long-sightedness (hypermetropia) the eyeball is short or the lens is too weak, so the image of a near object forms behind the retina. A convex lens corrects it.

s: The lens-type commonly used for correcting presbyopia is ………
x: Presbyopia is age-related loss of near vision, and in many cases distance vision also needs correction. Bifocal lenses, which combine concave and convex parts, are commonly used for it.

s: The SI unit of electric charge is
x: The SI unit of electric charge is the coulomb (1 C = charge of about 6.25 × 10¹⁸ electrons). Volt is potential difference, ampere current and ohm resistance.

s: ……… is the “work done in moving a unit charge between two points in an electric circuit.”
x: Potential difference is defined as the work done per unit charge in moving it between two points in a circuit. Current, power and resistance are defined differently.

s: The frequency of direct current ………
x: Direct current flows steadily in one direction and does not alternate. Its frequency is therefore zero, unlike AC (50 Hz in India).

s: Ohm’s law states the relation between ……… and ……… .
x: Ohm's law relates potential difference (V) and current (I) through a conductor: V = IR at constant temperature.

s: Which one of the following statements regarding Ohm’s law is not correct?
o: Ohm’s law is an assumption that current through a conductor is always directly proportional to the potential difference applied to it.
A conducting device obeys Ohm’s law when the resistance of a device is independent of magnitude and polarity of applied potential difference.
A conducting material obeys Ohm’s law when the resistance of material is independent of the magnitude and direction of applied electric field.
All homogeneous materials obey Ohm’s law irrespective of whether the field is within range or strong.
x: Ohm's law is not universal. Many materials and devices (semiconductors, diodes, strong fields) deviate from it, so the claim that all homogeneous materials obey it is wrong.

s: What is the SI unit of electrical resistance?
x: Resistance is measured in ohms. Volt is potential difference and ampere is current.

s: Two wires are made having same length l and area of cross-section A. Wire 1 is made of copper and wire 2 is made of aluminium. It is given that the electrical conductivity of copper is more than that of aluminium. In this context, which one of the following statements is correct?
o: The resistance of wire 1 will be higher than that of wire 2.
The resistance of wire 2 will be higher than that of wire 1.
The resistance of both the wires will be the same.
If same current is flown through both the wires, the power dissipated in both the wires will be the same.
x: Resistivity is the inverse of conductivity, and R = ρl/A. With the same l and A, aluminium has lower conductivity, so it has higher resistivity and higher resistance than copper.

s: A wire bound standard resistor uses manganin or constantan. It is because
o: these alloys are cheap and easily available.
they have resistivity which almost remains unchanged with temperature.
x: Manganin and constantan have resistivity that is almost unchanged with temperature. This is why they are used in standard resistors.

s: Superconductors are substances which
o: offer high resistance to the flow of current.
offer no resistance to the flow of current.
x: Superconductors offer no (zero) resistance to current below their critical temperature. 'Conduct at lower temperature' is vague and every conductor does that; 'high resistance' is the opposite.

s: When two resistors are connected in parallel, have ……… .
o: Both same current and different potential difference
x: Resistors in parallel are connected across the same two points. They therefore have the same potential difference, while the current divides.

s: The metal cap of an electric cell is generally the ……… terminal of the electrical cell.
x: The metal cap of a dry cell is its positive terminal, and the zinc case is the negative terminal.

s: Which of the following instruments is used to measure electric current?
x: An ammeter, connected in series, measures electric current. A voltmeter measures potential difference. A galvanometer only detects small currents.

s: The instrument used for detecting the presence of electric current in a circuit is
x: A galvanometer detects small electric currents in a circuit; refractometer, viscometer and diffractometer measure refractive index, viscosity and diffraction, so they cannot detect current.

s: The property of electric current which is applicable in the fuse wire is
x: A fuse works on the heating effect of current: the low-melting wire heats up and melts when current is excessive, breaking the circuit.

s: When a bar magnet is cut into two equal halves, the pole strength of each piece
x: Cutting a magnet always produces two complete magnets, each with north and south poles, because poles cannot be isolated. Each piece keeps the same pole strength, though its magnetic moment is halved.

s: The latest discovered state of matter is
x: Bose-Einstein condensate is the 5th and most recently discovered state of matter, after solid, liquid, gas and plasma.

s: The temperature at which a solid melts to become a liquid at the atmospheric pressure is called its melting point. The melting point of a solid is an indication of
o: strength of the intermolecular forces of attraction.
strength of the intermolecular forces of repulsion.
x: Melting requires overcoming the attractive forces holding particles together, so a higher melting point means stronger intermolecular forces of attraction.

s: Why do two ice blocks join to form one block when pressed together ?
o: Melting point of ice is lowered with increase in pressure.
Melting point of ice increases with increase in pressure.
Melting point of ice remains unchanged with increase in pressure.
x: Pressure lowers the melting point of ice, so ice at the contact surfaces melts under pressure and refreezes when pressure is released, joining the blocks (regelation).

s: Distant objects can be seen with the help of
x: A telescope uses a convex lens or mirror to form images of distant objects; a microscope is for tiny nearby objects.

s: Which one of the following has highest frequency?
x: Cosmic rays have the shortest wavelength and so the highest frequency among the options, higher than X-rays, microwaves and radio waves.

s: Which is the most suitable unit for expressing nuclear radius?
x: Nuclear radii are of the order of 10^-15 m, which is one fermi (femtometre), so fermi is the suitable unit.

s: The device used for measuring the wavelength of X-rays is
x: A Bragg spectrometer uses X-ray diffraction from crystal planes (nλ = 2d sinθ) to measure X-ray wavelength. A GM counter only detects radiation, a cyclotron accelerates particles, and a mass spectrometer measures mass.

s: Which one of the following does not convert electrical energy into light energy?
x: A candle produces light by burning, i.e. chemical energy. LED (electroluminescence), laser and TV convert electrical energy to light.

s: The speed of sound in air at 0°C is
x: The speed of sound in air at 0°C is about 331 m/s, written 331 ms⁻¹ with the correct unit.

s: Which law of physics states that the force between the two electric charges reduces to a quarter of its former value when the distance between them is doubled?
x: Coulomb's law says force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance, so doubling the distance reduces the force to one quarter.

s: In step-down transformer, the AC output gives the
o: current more than the input current.
current less than the input current.
current equal to the input current.
voltage more than the input voltage.
x: A step-down transformer lowers voltage and, since power is nearly conserved, raises current, so output current is greater than input current. It works only on AC.

s: The SI unit of acceleration is
x: Acceleration is change in velocity (m/s) per unit time (s), so its SI unit is m/s², i.e. ms-2.

s: Which one of the following physical quantities does not affect the resistance of a cylindrical resistor?
o: The resistivity of the material used in the resistor.
The area of cross-section of the cylinder.
x: Resistance R = ρl/A depends on resistivity, length and cross-sectional area, not on the current passing through it.

s: Which one among the following components is used as an amplifying device?
x: A transistor can amplify signals; a transformer changes AC voltage, a diode rectifies and a capacitor stores charge.

s: Radioactive elements emit
x: Radioactive elements spontaneously emit alpha, beta and gamma radiations, not radio, infrared or ultraviolet waves.

s: Which of the following phenomena is involved in Kaleidoscope?
x: A kaleidoscope uses multiple reflections from inclined mirrors to form symmetric patterns.

s: According to law of reflection
o: Angle of incidence is greater than angle of reflection.
Angle of incidence is smaller than angle of reflection.
Angle of incidence is always equal to angle of reflection.
x: The law of reflection states that the angle of incidence always equals the angle of reflection.

s: A person holding a pen in his left hand sees his reflection in the mirror holding the pen in his right hand. This is due to which of the following phenomena?
x: A plane mirror reverses left and right in the image, which is called lateral inversion.

s: When a ray of light travel from a denser medium to a rarer medium, it bends
o: towards the normal and slows down.
away from the normal and speeds up.
away from the normal and slows down.
towards the normal and speeds up.
x: Going from a denser to a rarer medium, light speeds up and bends away from the normal.

s: The absolute refractive index of air is
x: The absolute refractive index of air is about 1.0003.

s: An oscilloscope is an instrument which allows us to see waves produced by
x: An oscilloscope displays electrical signals; it is used to view sound waves (converted by a microphone) as waveforms.

s: If an object moves at a non-zero constant acceleration for a certain interval of time, then the distance it covers in that time
o: is independent of its initial velocity.
x: With constant acceleration, s = ut + ½at², so the distance covered depends on the initial velocity u.

s: The absolute zero is a temperature at which ………
o: molecular motion in a gas would cease
x: Absolute zero (0 K) is the temperature at which molecular motion would cease.

s: Why is it difficult to measure the coefficient of expansion of a liquid than solid?
o: Liquids tend to evaporate at all temperatures.
Liquids expand too much when heated.
Their containers also expand when heated.
x: The container also expands on heating, so the observed liquid expansion is only apparent, which makes measuring it difficult.

s: What is sublimation?
o: It is the process of conversion of a liquid into gas.
It is the process of conversion of a solid into liquid.
It is the process of conversion of a solid into vapour.
It is the process of conversion of a gas into liquid.
x: Sublimation is the direct change of a solid into vapour without passing through the liquid state.

s: Matter around us can exist in three different states, namely, solid, liquid and gas. The correct order of their compressibility is
x: Compressibility is lowest in solids and highest in gases, so Solid < Liquid < Gas.

s:
Match the following. Process Changes

A. Evaporation
1. Liquid into gas

B. Sublimation
2. Solid into gas

C. Freezing
3. Solid into liquid

D. Melting
4. Liquid into solid
Codes A B C D A B C D
x: Evaporation is liquid to gas, sublimation solid to gas, freezing liquid to solid and melting solid to liquid, giving 1 2 4 3.

s: Which one of the following is not the result of surface tension?
o: Vapour formation above the liquid surface.
Spherical shape of mercury fallen on the floor.
x: Surface tension explains the meniscus shape, capillary rise and spherical mercury drops. Vapour formation is evaporation, which is a separate process and not a result of surface tension.

s: Which one of the following statement about the mass of a body is correct?
o: It changes from one place to another.
It does not depend on its temperature.
x: Mass is the amount of matter in a body and is the same everywhere; weight (mg) changes with place. Mass does not change with location or shape, so 'same everywhere' is the intended answer.

s: Which one among the following transitions of electron of hydrogen atom emits radiation of the shortest wavelength?
x: Shortest wavelength means the largest energy gap. The n=2 to n=1 transition has the biggest gap among the options, so it emits the shortest wavelength.

s: Infrared, visible and ultraviolet radiations/ light have different properties. Which one of the following statements related to these radiations/light is not correct?
o: The wavelength of infrared is more than that of ultraviolet radiation.
The wavelength of ultraviolet is smaller than that of visible light.
The photon energy of visible light is more than that of infrared light.
The photon energy of ultraviolet is less than that of visible light.
x: Ultraviolet has a shorter wavelength than visible light, so its photon energy is higher. Statement 4 says it is lower, so it is the incorrect one.

s: In which region of electromagnetic spectrum does the Lyman series of hydrogen atom lie?
x: The Lyman series involves transitions to n=1, which emit high-energy photons in the ultraviolet region.

s: A photon of X-ray has energy of 1 keV. A photon of visible radiation has energy of 3 eV. In this context, which one of the following statement(s) is/are not correct?
o: The wavelength of X-ray photon is less than the wavelength of visible radiation photon.
Both the photons have different energies.
The speeds of both the photons in vacuum are different.
The frequency of X-ray photon is higher than the frequency of visible radiation photon.
x: All photons travel at the speed of light in vacuum, whatever their energy. So the claim that the two speeds differ is wrong.

s: What is weight?
o: Weight can be determined by only a spring balance.
The weight of a body is constant.
The force with which earth attracts towards its centre.
Weight of a body has a direction towards the centre of the earth. So it is a vector quantity.
x: Weight is the force with which the earth attracts a body towards its centre, which is the definition asked. Weight is not constant (it varies with place) and can be measured by other balances too; its direction towards the centre is a property, not the definition.

s: The weight of a body at the centre of Earth is
o: half the weight at the surface
twice the weight at the surface
x: At the centre of the Earth, g is zero because the attractions cancel out, so the weight is zero.

s: The weight of an object on the moon is equal ……… of its weight on the earth.
x: The moon's gravity is about one sixth of the earth's, so weight on the moon is 1/6th of that on earth.

s: Which term is not associated with sound wave?
x: Candela is the unit of luminous intensity, so it is not related to sound. Hertz (frequency), decibel (loudness) and Mach (speed relative to sound) are all linked to sound.

s: The speed of a body that has mach number more than 1 is
x: Mach number is the ratio of a body's speed to the speed of sound. A value above 1 means the speed is supersonic.

s: When a ray of light enters a glass slab, then
x: Frequency is set by the source and does not change on entering a new medium. Velocity and wavelength change instead.

s: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities have the same dimensions?
x: Work and energy both have the dimensions ML²T⁻². Power has different dimensions.

s: Which one of the following can charge an insulator?
x: An insulator holds charge only on its surface, so it is charged by static electricity, i.e. by rubbing (friction). Current electricity needs a conductor, and magnetic or gravitational fields do not charge a body.

s: In the equation of motion v = u + at , u represents ........... .
x: In v = u + at, u is the initial velocity and v is the final velocity.

s:
Consider the following statements.

I. There is no net moment on a body which is in equilibrium.

II. The momentum of a body is always conserved.

III. The kinetic energy of an object is always conserved.
Which of the statements (s) given above is/are correct?
x: Only statement I is correct: in equilibrium the net moment is zero. Momentum is conserved only when no external force acts, and kinetic energy is not conserved in inelastic collisions.

s: Sound is a form of …… that produces sensation of hearing.
x: Sound is a mechanical wave produced by vibrations and needs a medium, so it is mechanical energy, not an electromagnetic wave.

s: If the work done on the system or by the system is zero, then which one of the following statement for a gas kept at a certain temperature is correct?
o: Change in internal energy of the system is equal to flow of the heat in or out of the system.
Change in internal energy of the system is less than heat transferred.
Change in internal energy of the system is more than the heat flow.
x: By the first law, ΔU = Q - W. With W = 0, ΔU = Q, so the change in internal energy equals the heat flow.

s: Which phenomena shows the particle nature of light?
x: The photoelectric effect is explained by light as photons (particles). Diffraction, interference and polarisation show its wave nature.

s:
An electron and a proton starting from rest are accelerated through a potential difference of 1000 V.
Which one of the following statements in this regard is correct?
o: The kinetic energy of both the particles will be different.
The speed of the electron will be higher than that of the proton.
The speed of the proton will be higher than that of the electron.
The speed of the electron and the proton will be equal.
x: Both gain the same kinetic energy (qV), as the charges are equal in magnitude. Since KE = ½mv², the lighter electron gets the higher speed.

s: When a longitudinal wave moves through a certain medium; the quantity which is transmitted through the medium is
o: both material of the medium and energy
x: A wave transmits only energy through the medium; the particles just oscillate about their mean positions and the material is not carried along.

s: The average kinetic energy of the molecules of an ideal gas is directly proportional to
x: By kinetic theory, the average kinetic energy of ideal gas molecules is (3/2)kT, proportional to the absolute temperature.

s: The light is composed of small particles, called ………
x: Light consists of packets of energy called photons, as in the quantum theory of light.

s: In a bi-polar junction transistor,
o: all the three regions (the emitter, the base and the collector) have equal concentrations of impurity.
the emitter has the least concentration of impurity.
the collector has the least concentration of impurity.
the base has the least concentration of impurity.
x: In a BJT the base is thin and lightly doped, the emitter is heavily doped and the collector is moderately doped.

s: Which of the following is widely used in making semiconductor chips?
x: Germanium is a metalloid semiconductor used in chips (with silicon); radium, sodium and sulphur are not used for this.

s: The unit for measurement of energy is
x: The joule is the SI unit of energy. The calorie is also an energy unit, but not the SI one; pascal is pressure and horsepower is power.

s: What is the name of the device used to convert alternating current into direct current?
x: A rectifier (using diodes) converts AC into DC; a transformer only changes AC voltage.

s: Which one of the following devices changes low voltage alternating current to high voltage alternating current and vice-versa?
x: A transformer steps AC voltage up or down by electromagnetic (mutual) induction and works only on AC. A generator makes electricity and a motor turns it into motion.

s: Which one of the following statements is correct with regard to the material of electrical insulators?
o: Electrons do not flow easily through them.
They have more number of electrons than the protons on their surface.
x: Insulators have electrons, but they are tightly bound and do not flow easily; so option 2 is right.

s: A body is charged negatively. It implies that
o: it has lost some of its protons.
it has lost some of its electrons.
it has gained some electrons from outside.
x: A body becomes negatively charged by gaining electrons; protons are not transferred in charging.

s: Process of gaining electrons is known as ……… .
x: By OIL RIG, oxidation is electron loss, so gain of electrons is reduction.

s: The ionisation energy of hydrogen atom in the ground state is
x: The energy needed to remove the electron from hydrogen's ground state is 13.6 eV (electron-volts), not MeV or J.

s: Creation of something from nothing is against the law of
x: Creating something from nothing would violate the law of conservation of mass-energy, which says mass-energy can be neither created nor destroyed.

s: “The sum of emf’s and potential differences around a closed loop equals zero” is a consequence of
x: Kirchhoff's loop rule says the net energy gained and lost by a charge around a closed loop is zero, which is conservation of energy.

s: When a beam of white light is allowed to fall on a prism, the maximum deviation of the emerging light occurs for
x: Violet light has the shortest wavelength and highest refractive index in glass, so it bends (deviates) the most in a prism; red deviates the least.

s: The first law of thermodynamics is simply the case of
o: The Law of Conservation of Energy
x: The first law of thermodynamics states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, which is the law of conservation of energy applied to heat and work.

s: The statement that ‘heat cannot flow by itself from a body at a lower temperature to a body at a higher temperature’, is known as
x: The Kelvin-Clausius statement that heat cannot flow spontaneously from cold to hot body is the Second Law of Thermodynamics.

s: When sound waves are propagated through a medium, the physical quantity/quantities transmitted is/are
x: Sound waves transmit only energy through a medium; the particles just oscillate about their mean positions and no matter is carried along.

s: What is the process of transferring of charge from a charged object to the Earth called?
x: Transferring charge from a charged body to the Earth is called earthing (grounding).

s: Where is a transistor most likely to be found?
x: Transistors are used in amplifier circuits such as hearing aids. A fuse is a simple heating-effect wire and a fluorescent lamp is a gas discharge tube.

s: When X -rays are produced
o: heat is generated at the target.
heat is absorbed at the target.
the temperature of the target remains constant.
brilliant light is seen at the target.
x: In an X-ray tube only about 1% of the electron energy becomes X-rays, and the rest is converted to heat at the target, so heat is generated there.

s: If the potential difference applied to an X-ray tube is doubled while keeping the separation between the filament and the target as same, what will happen to the cut-off wavelength?
o: Will be four times of the original wavelength
x: The cut-off wavelength is λ = hc/eV, so it is inversely proportional to the applied potential; doubling V halves the cut-off wavelength.

s: Which one of the following statement with regarding to expansion of materials due to heating is not correct?
o: As ice melts, it expands uniformly upto 4°C.
Mercury thermometer works using the principle of expansion due to heating.
Small gap is kept between two rails to allow for expansion due to heating.
The length of metallic wire increases when its temperature is increased.
x: Water contracts, not expands, when heated from 0°C to 4°C (anomalous expansion of water), so the statement about ice expanding uniformly up to 4°C is incorrect.

s: Which one of the following will happen if the medium surrounding the cell has a higher concentration than the cell?
x: Water moves by osmosis from low to high solute concentration through a semi-permeable membrane. A cell in a more concentrated medium therefore loses water and shrinks.

s: Electron emission from a metallic surface by the application of light is known as
x: Emission of electrons from a metal surface by incident light is the photoelectric effect. Thermionic emission is caused by heat.

s: Three resistors with magnitudes 2, 4 and 8 Ω are connected in parallel, then equivalent resistance of the system would be
o: more than 2 Ω but less than 4 Ω
x: In parallel the equivalent resistance is less than the smallest resistor. 1/R = 1/2+1/4+1/8 = 7/8, so R = 8/7 Ω, which is less than 2 Ω.

s: When resistors are connected in series, then net resistance ……… .
x: In series the resistances add up, Rs = R1+R2+..., so the net resistance increases.

s: While moving from one end to another end inside a solenoid, its magnetic field ……… .
x: Inside a solenoid the magnetic field is uniform, with parallel field lines, so it remains the same.

s: What will be the focal length when human eye lens becomes thin?
x: A thinner eye lens is less converging, so its focal length increases. A thicker lens has a shorter focal length.

s: What is measured in hertz?
x: Hertz is the SI unit of frequency, equal to one cycle per second.

s: On a cold day when the room temperature is 15°C, the metallic cap of a pen becomes much colder than its plastic body, though both are at the same temperature of 15°C, because
o: metals have higher thermal capacity than plastics.
plastics have a lower density than metals.
metals are good conductors of heat.
plastics have a higher thermal conductivity than metals.
x: Metal is a good conductor, so it draws heat from the hand quickly and feels colder than plastic, a poor conductor, at the same temperature.

s: Red + Green + Blue = ?
x: Red, green and blue are the primary colours of light, and mixing all three gives white light.

s: Which colour is formed when Red and Green are mixed?
x: Mixing red and green light gives yellow, as in additive colour mixing.

s: The primary colours in photography are
x: The primary colours of light, used in photography, are red, green and blue. Yellow and cyan are secondary colours.

s: Ultrasonic waves are produced by making use of
x: Ultrasonic waves are generated by the piezoelectric effect: a quartz crystal vibrates at high frequency when an alternating voltage is applied to it.

s:
Two long wires each carrying a current in the same direction are placed close to each other.
Which one of the following statement is correct?
o: The wires will attract with each other.
The wires will repel with each other.
There will be no force between the wires.
There will be a force between the wires only at the moment when the current is switched ON or OFF.
x: Parallel currents in the same direction produce magnetic fields that make the wires attract each other; opposite currents would repel.

s: Which one of the following is an ohmic conductor?
x: An ohmic conductor obeys Ohm's law (V proportional to I). Metals like silver do; semiconductors such as germanium and silicon and carbon do not follow it.

s: The product of conductivity and resistivity of a conductor
o: depends on current flowing through conductor.
is the same for all conductors.
x: Conductivity is the reciprocal of resistivity (σ = 1/ρ), so their product is always 1 for every conductor.

s: Wires in our homes are made of metal because metals are
x: Metals have free electrons and are good conductors of electricity, so they carry current with little loss; this is why household wires are metal.

s: Which of the following is not one of the fundamental quantities in Physics?
x: Length, time and mass are fundamental quantities; weight is a force (mg), a derived quantity that varies with gravity.

s: Angstrom is a unit of
x: The angstrom is 10⁻¹⁰ m, a unit of length used for wavelengths and atomic sizes. Energy is in joules or eV, frequency in hertz, velocity in m/s.

s:
Assertion (A) A piece of ice added to drink, cools it.
Reason (R) Ice takes latent heat from the drink for melting resulting the cooling of the drink.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Ice absorbs latent heat of fusion from the drink while melting, which lowers the drink's temperature, so R correctly explains A.

s:
Mass of a particular amount of substance

I. is the amount of matter present in it.

II. does not vary from place to place.

III. changes with change in gravitational force.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below
x: Mass measures the amount of matter (inertia) and is constant everywhere; only weight changes with gravity, so III is wrong.

s:
Water is heated with a coil of resistance R connected to domestic supply. The rise of temperature of water will depend on

I. supply voltage.

II. current passing through the coil.

III. time for which voltage is supplied.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Heat produced is H = V²t/R = I²Rt, so it depends on voltage, current and time, making all three statements correct.

s: What is the unit of pressure?
x: Pressure is force per unit area, so its unit is N/m², called the pascal.

s: Which of the following radiation is used to get relief from body aches ?
x: Infrared rays warm the tissues and are used in physiotherapy for body aches. UV is used for sterilisation, and visible light has no such heating use.

s:
Consider the following
Assertion (A) and
Reason (R) and choose your answer from the given code :
Assertion (A) : The upper surface of the wings of an aeroplane is made convex and the lower surface is made concave.
Reason (R) : The air current at the top has less velocity and thus less pressure at the bottom than at the top.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
x: A is true: the wing's convex top makes air move faster above it. R is false because faster air on top means lower pressure on top than below, which gives lift.

s:
Consider the following Assertion and
Reason:
1.
Assertion (A): In the visible spectrum of light, red light is more energetic than green light.
2.
Reason (R): The wavelength of red light is more than that of green light.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are individually true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: A is false: red light is less energetic than green light. R is true: red light (~700 nm) has a longer wavelength than green (~530 nm), and energy falls as wavelength rises.

s:
Assertion (A): With the increase of temperature, the viscosity of glycerin increases.
Reason (R) : Rise of temperature increases kinetic energy of molecules.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
x: A is false because a liquid's viscosity, glycerin's included, falls as it warms. R is true: heating raises the molecules' kinetic energy, which is why the viscosity falls.

s:
Assertion (A) : In a motion picture, usually 24 frames are projected every second over the whole length of the film.
