x: Active transport moves a substance against its concentration gradient using energy (ATP) from respiration; movement along the gradient or without energy is diffusion or passive transport.

s: Process by which plant prepare their food is
x: Plants prepare their food by photosynthesis, using light, CO2 and water in chlorophyll-containing cells.

s: Which of the following organelles of a cell is/are involved in photosynthesis ?
x: Photosynthesis occurs in chloroplasts, which contain chlorophyll; mitochondria are for respiration.

s: The increase in length of stems and roots in plants is due to
x: Apical meristems at the tips of stems and roots cause increase in length (primary growth); lateral meristem increases girth.

s: Which one of the following organisms has vascular tissues ?
x: Marsilea is a pteridophyte and has xylem and phloem. Cladophora and Anabaena are algae and Penicillium is a fungus, so none of them has vascular tissue.

s: Marsilea, fern and horse tail are examples of which one of the following plant groups ?
x: Marsilea, ferns and horsetails (Equisetum) are all seedless vascular plants, so they belong to Pteridophyta.

s: In the plant kingdom, ferns and fern allies belong to which group ?
x: Ferns and fern allies (horsetails, club mosses) make up the Pteridophyta.

s: Which of the following is/are the main absorbing organ/organs of plants?
x: Roots are the main absorbing organs of plants, taking up water and minerals from the soil through root hairs.

s: Which one of the following statements about classification of plants is correct?
o: Thallophytes have well differentiated body design.
Vascular system is not found among Bryophytes.
x: Bryophytes lack a vascular system (xylem and phloem). Thallophytes lack a differentiated body, Funaria is a moss, and pteridophytes are cryptogams, not phanerogams.

s: Pteridophytes are also known as
x: Pteridophytes have vascular tissue but no seeds or flowers, so they are called vascular cryptogams.

s: The nature of stele in primitive vascular plants was
x: Primitive vascular plants had a protostele, in which the xylem forms a solid core surrounded by phloem.

s: A flower is a modified
x: A flower is a modified shoot, formed from the shoot apical meristem, with its parts as modified leaves.

s: Gymnosperms are characterised by
x: Gymnosperms (e.g., pines, cycads) bear naked seeds not enclosed in an ovary or fruit; angiosperms have seeds inside fruits.

s: First compound which is fixed during photosynthesis is
x: In the Calvin cycle CO2 combines with RuBP to give 3-phosphoglyceric acid (PGA), the first stable product of carbon fixation. Glucose and starch form later.

s: Which one of the following is not used as fertiliser?
x: Ammonium nitrate, phosphate and sulphate supply nitrogen or phosphorus to crops and are fertilisers. Ammonium sulphide is not used as one.

s: An element present in Chlorophyll is
x: Chlorophyll has magnesium at the centre of its porphyrin ring.

s: Double fertilisation occurs among
x: Double fertilisation, in which one sperm fuses with the egg and the other with the polar nuclei, is unique to angiosperms.

s: The technique of the development of fruits without fertilisation is known as
x: Parthenocarpy is the development of fruit without fertilisation, giving seedless fruit. Parthenogenesis is the development of an embryo from an unfertilised egg, not of a fruit.

s: The development of a fruit without fertilisation is called …
x: Parthenocarpy is fruit development without fertilisation. Apomixis is seed formation without fertilisation, so it is not the answer.

s: Which of the following is correct sequence of the events occurring during sexual reproduction in plants?
o: Seedling, Embryo formation, Pollination, Fertilisation, Division of zygote
Embryo formation, seedling, Pollination, Fertilisation, Division of zygote
Pollination, Fertilisation, Division of zygote, Embryo formation, Seedling
Seedling, Embryo formation, Division of zygote, Pollination, Fertilisation
x: In plant sexual reproduction, pollination is followed by fertilisation, then division of the zygote, embryo formation and finally the seedling.

s: Which one of the following statements about meristematic tissue in plants is correct?
o: These are dead tissues and from wood.
They provide flexibility to plant due to their thickened walls.
These are present is the bark of a tree only.
Growth occurs in plants due to division of cells of these tissues.
x: Meristematic tissue is made of actively dividing cells, and its cell division drives plant growth. It is not dead and is not limited to bark.

s: Which one of the following plant tissues has dead cells?
x: Sclerenchyma cells have thick lignified walls and are dead at maturity. Epidermis, parenchyma and collenchyma are living tissues.

s: The hormone related to drought tolerance is
x: Abscisic acid is the stress hormone. It closes stomata and so helps the plant tolerate drought.

s: Which one of the following agents does not contribute to propagation of plants through seed dispersal ?
x: Seeds are dispersed by wind, water and animals. Fungi do not disperse seeds.

s: The maximum amount of water, which plants need to grow, is absorbed by the following?
x: Root hairs are the main water-absorbing part of the root; water enters them by osmosis from the soil, so they absorb the most water for the plant.

s: Which among the following is an example of dicot seed?
x: Pulses (legumes) have two cotyledons so they are dicots; rice, wheat and maize are monocot cereals.

s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct regarding vegetative propagation of plants ?

I. Vegetative propagation produces clonal population.

II. Vegetative propagation helps in eliminating the virus.

III. Vegetative propagation can be practised most of the year.
Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
x: Vegetative propagation gives clones (I) and can be done through much of the year (III). It does not eliminate viruses, since the virus passes on to the offspring, so II is wrong.

s: The by-product of photosynthesis is
x: In photosynthesis, water is split and oxygen is released as the by-product; sugar is the main product, and CO2 is a raw material.

s: Essential requirements for a seed to germinate
x: A seed needs water, air (oxygen) and a suitable temperature to germinate. Soil and sunlight are not essential; seeds sprout on wet cotton in the dark.

s: Siphoning type of mouth parts are present in:
x: A butterfly has a long coiled proboscis for siphoning nectar. The mosquito pierces and sucks, the cockroach chews and the housefly sponges.

s: It is harmful to sleep under a tree at night because the tree releases :
x: At night trees cannot photosynthesise but keep respiring, so they release carbon dioxide. They do not give out carbon monoxide or sulphur dioxide.

s: Which light is most effective in photosynthesis?
x: Red light (~655 nm) gives the highest rate of photosynthesis. Blue is also absorbed, but green is mostly reflected.

s: Chlorophyll absorbs ____ wavelengths of the sunlight.
o: More than one of the above
x: Chlorophyll absorbs mainly red and blue light and reflects green, which is why leaves look green. Options with green are therefore wrong.

s: Which of the following has the shortest gestation period?

s: Which animal can not digest fibres properly ?
x: The pig is a monogastric omnivore and cannot digest fibre well. Goats and cows are ruminants, and elephants are hindgut fermenters, so their gut microbes break down cellulose.

s: Desert plants have longer root system because :

Roots grow in search of water
Soil does not contain water, hence becomes compact
Roots moves opposite to the solar heat

s: In a bisexual flower, if androecium and gynoecium mature at different times, the phenomenon is known as

s: Which of the following elements is not essential for plant growth ?

s: Eight nucleated female gametophyte is found in

s: Among living organisms, which one of the following is the most responsible factor for bringing about the origin of a new species?
x:
Official key / most books: mutation. Strictly: mutation supplies variation, while reproductive isolation is what actually completes speciation (NCERT Biology XII ch.6).
Books and keys give mutation (de Vries) as the source of new heritable variation that leads to new species.

s: World first Camel hospital is located in which city?

s: In the context of organic evolution, the loss of limbs in snakes is explained by the phenomenon of
x:
Official key / most books: use and disuse of organs (Lamarck). Strictly: modern biology explains it by natural selection; Lamarckism is rejected (NCERT Biology XII ch.6).
Books and the key explain limb loss in snakes by Lamarck's use and disuse of organs.

s: Which one of the following elements is present in the green pigment of leaves?
x: Chlorophyll has a magnesium atom at the centre of its porphyrin ring (haemoglobin has iron).

s: Solar energy is converted into ATP in
x: In chloroplasts the light reactions convert solar energy into ATP (photophosphorylation) and NADPH; mitochondria make ATP from food, not from sunlight.

s: World’s first camel hospital is located in which city?
x: The Dubai Camel Hospital (opened 2017) is billed as the world's first dedicated camel hospital.

s: The reason of large scale diversity among the organisms is
x:

Books and the BPSC key give adaptation – organisms adapting to varied environments – as the reason for large-scale diversity.

s: Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to stigma of another flower of the same plant is called ?
x: Geitonogamy = pollen to another flower of the same plant; autogamy – same flower; xenogamy – a different plant.

s:
Consider the following statements

I. Homologous organs are common origin with different functions.

II. Analogous organs are different origin but perform similar function in different organisms.

III. Vestigial organs are non-functional and rudimentary organs in an organism which are fully developed and functional in phylogenetically related organisms.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
x: All three are correct definitions: homologous – same origin, different function; analogous – different origin, same function; vestigial – rudimentary organs functional in relatives.

s: Which of the following is poisonous for dogs?
x: Chocolate contains theobromine, which dogs metabolise slowly, so it is toxic to them.

s: The broad, green part of the leaf is called
x: The lamina (leaf blade) is the broad green part where most photosynthesis occurs; midrib – central vein, petiole – stalk, stipules – basal outgrowths.

s: The broad , green part of the leaf is called
x: The lamina (leaf blade) is the broad green part; the petiole is the stalk, midrib and veins conduct and support.

s: At what age does bamboo flower?
x:
Printed key / books: 30 years. Strictly: it depends on the species – Melocanna baccifera (Mizoram mautam) flowers about every 48 years; PMF Part 3 p.34 says 50–100 years.
Bamboos flower only once, after long, species-specific intervals; the key takes about 30 years (Melocanna bambusoides ~30–35 years).

s: Maximum Photosynthesis occurs in:
x: Photosynthesis is highest in red light (with a second peak in blue), which chlorophyll absorbs most efficiently.

s: Pigment without oxygen is:
x: Carotenes are pure hydrocarbons (C40H56) with no oxygen; xanthophylls are their oxygenated forms, and chlorophyll and phycobilins contain oxygen.

s: To which group of plants does the Banyan Tree belong?
x: The banyan (Ficus benghalensis) is a flowering, fruit-bearing plant – an angiosperm.

s: In plants, active cell division occurs in the following parts
x: Active division takes place in meristems; among the options the root tip (root apical meristem, the classic onion-root-tip mitosis slide) is the expected answer.

x: Vitamin D is made in the skin on exposure to sunlight, so it is called the sunshine vitamin. Vitamins A, C and K are not made this way.

s: Vitamin related with production of antibodies is:

s: Which of the following is/are a source of Vitamin K?
x:
APPSC 2004 key: nuts, eggs, liver. Strictly, green leafy vegetables are the richest source of vitamin K (PMF General Science Part 3 p.14), but option (c) adds tomatoes and carrots, which are poor sources.
Nuts, eggs and animal liver supply vitamin K, which is the exam key. Green leafy vegetables are the best-known source, but tomatoes and carrots are poor, so option (c) is not a clean answer; shark-liver oil gives vitamins A and D.

s: Which of the following are water-soluble vitamins ?
x: B-group vitamins and vitamin C are water-soluble; A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, so every pair with A or D is wrong.

s: Golden Rice is a rich source of :
x: Golden Rice is genetically engineered to make beta-carotene, the precursor of vitamin A, in the grain.

s: Scurvy is a disease caused by the deficiency of :
x: Scurvy (bleeding gums, poor wound healing) is caused by lack of vitamin C (ascorbic acid). B2 deficiency causes cheilosis and vitamin A deficiency night blindness.

s: Which of the following vitamins contains cobalt?
x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) is the only vitamin with a metal – cobalt – at its centre. K, B6 and B2 contain no cobalt.

s: A person will suffer from beri-beri, rickets and scurvy if he is not taking adequate amounts of :
x: Beri-beri = lack of B1 (thiamine), rickets = lack of D, scurvy = lack of C, so B1, D and C. The other sets include vitamins (A, E, K, B6) linked to other diseases.

s: Which of the following vitamin helps in blood clotting in humans?
x: Vitamin K is needed to make clotting factors (prothrombin), so it helps blood clot. A is for vision, D for bones.

s: Which of the following vitamins is essential for normal vision?
x: Retinol (vitamin A) forms the visual pigment rhodopsin, so it is essential for normal vision. Folic acid, riboflavin and niacin are B vitamins with other roles.

s: Which of the following pairs is not correctly matched?
x: Tocopherol (vitamin E) deficiency causes sterility and muscle weakness; beri-beri is due to thiamine (B1). The other three pairs are correct.

s:
Consider the following pairs : Vitamin Deficiency disease
1. Vitamin C : Scurvy
2. Vitamin D : Rickets
3. Vitamin E : Night blindness Which of the pairs given above is/are correctly matched?
x: Vitamin C – scurvy and vitamin D – rickets are correct; night blindness is due to vitamin A, not E (E deficiency causes sterility/muscle weakness).

s: Which one of the following vitamins is helpful in keeping a dream in memory for a longer duration?
x: Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) was found (University of Adelaide study, 2018) to improve people's ability to recall their dreams. Vitamins A, D and C have no such link.

s: Which one of the following compounds is not a vitamin?
x: Thyroxine is a hormone of the thyroid gland, not a vitamin. Niacin (B3), riboflavin (B2) and pyridoxine (B6) are B vitamins.

s: Golden rice is a richer source of –
x: Golden Rice carries genes for beta-carotene (provitamin A), so it is a richer source of vitamin A; it was developed against vitamin A deficiency.

s: Which one of the following statements is not correct ?

Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency leads to the dry and

Vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency can lead to heart
x: Milk is a good source of riboflavin (B2) and B12, so 'milk contains none of the B vitamins' is wrong. Vitamin A lack causes dry eyes, scurvy causes joint pain and thiamine lack (wet beri-beri) can cause heart failure.

s: For which desirable character the transgenic crop ‘Golden Rice’ is produced ?
x: Golden Rice was engineered to produce beta-carotene (provitamin A) in the endosperm; it is not for amino acids, insulin or starch quality.

s: Which one of the following is an important source of vitamin E?
x: Wheat-germ oil is the richest natural source of vitamin E (tocopherol). Palm, coconut and mustard oil contain much less.

s: Which of the following vitamins is mainly responsible for blood coagulation in human being?
x: Vitamin K is needed for the liver to make prothrombin and other clotting factors; E, A and C have no direct role in coagulation.

s: Which of the following vitamin is effective in blood clotting?
x: Vitamin K (the 'koagulation' vitamin) makes blood clot; lack of it prolongs clotting time.

s: Which of the following vitamins contain cobalt –
x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) contains cobalt; B1, B2 and B6 contain no metal.

s: Deficiency of which vitamin can cause night blindness?
x: Vitamin A deficiency causes night blindness; B1 causes beri-beri, C scurvy and E sterility.

s: Which of the following has the highest content of Vitamin C ?
x: Guava has about 200+ mg vitamin C per 100 g, about four times an orange; carrot and mango are known for vitamin A.

s: Which one of the following vitamins is formed in skin in the presence of sunlight?
x: Vitamin D is made in the skin when UV-B in sunlight acts on 7-dehydrocholesterol – the 'sunshine vitamin'.

s: The main source of Vitamin ‘C’ is –
x: Vitamin C comes mainly from fresh raw fruits (amla, guava, citrus); it is destroyed by heat and milk, ghee and pulses are poor in it.

s: Cyanocobalamin is –
x: Cyanocobalamin is the cobalt-containing form of vitamin B12. Vitamin C is ascorbic acid, B2 riboflavin, B6 pyridoxine.

s: Which of the following vitamins are fat soluble?
x: A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, so A and D is the pair; C and B12 are water-soluble.

s: Riboflavin deficiency causes which of the following diseases?

s:

s: Which of the following vitamins is known as ergocalciferol?

s:

s: If a person only takes milk, egg and bread in diet, so he may suffer from the disease :

x: Vitamin C, found in citrus fruits, is needed for collagen and so for healthy skin and gums.

x: Vitamin A must come from food (retinol, or carotene converted in the gut/liver); proteins, enzymes and hormones are all synthesised in the body.

s: The common name of the chemical compound 'Cholecalciferol' is :
x: Cholecalciferol is vitamin D3, the form made in the skin under sunlight.

s: The vitamin which is effective in blood clotting is :
x: Vitamin K is needed for clotting factors; lack of it prolongs clotting.

s: Which of the following is the richest source of vitamin A?
x: Among the fruits given, mango is the richest in beta-carotene (vitamin A); papaya is close, while apple and guava are poor in it.

s: Use of polished rice in human diet causes the following disease
x: Polished rice has lost its thiamine-rich bran, so it causes beri-beri; goitre is iodine and night blindness vitamin A deficiency.

s: Some vitamins are fat soluble while others are water soluble. Which of the following are water soluble :
o: Vitamin A, D, E and K
x: Vitamins B and C are water-soluble; A, D, E and K are fat-soluble, so any set with A, D or K is wrong.

s: Among the following vegetables, the maximum Vitamin C is found in :
x: Green chilli has about 100+ mg vitamin C per 100 g, the most among these vegetables; pumpkin, pea and radish have far less.

s: Which of the following vitamin's deficiency causes disease of slow blood coagulation ?
x: Vitamin K deficiency increases clotting time (slow coagulation). C, D and E deficiencies cause scurvy, rickets and sterility.

s: Which one of the following contains more vitamin A content ?
x: Carrot is the richest in beta-carotene (vitamin A) of these vegetables, ahead of spinach; cabbage and cauliflower have little.

s: In countries where polished rice is the mean cereal in their diet, people suffer from –
x: Polished rice lacks thiamine (B1), so people eating it as the main cereal suffer beri-beri. Pellagra is a maize-diet (niacin) disease.

s: Which of the following is the richest source of Vitamin C?
x: Amla (Indian gooseberry) is the richest common source of vitamin C (~600 mg/100 g), far above orange; apple and carrot are poor.

s: The chemical name of Vitamin C is –
x: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid; thiamine is B1, while citric and tartaric acids are fruit acids, not vitamins.

s: Which one of the following is useful in the treatment of scurvy disease?
x: Aonla (amla, Indian gooseberry) is the richest vitamin C source, so it treats scurvy; mango and papaya have less and ber is moderate.

s: Which of the following statement regarding vitamin is not correct?
o: Some vitamins can be synthesised by intestinal microbes.
Some vitamins are stored in body.
vitamin K is a water soluble vitamin.
x: Vitamin K is fat-soluble, so that statement is wrong. Gut microbes make K and B12, vitamin D acts as a hormone, and fat-soluble vitamins and B12 are stored.

s: Vitamin C is also known as …………
x: Vitamin C is ascorbic acid; tartaric (tamarind), malic (apple) and acetic (vinegar) acids are not vitamins.

s: The deficiency of which nutrient causes night blindness?
x: Vitamin A (retinol) deficiency causes night blindness; K, C and protein deficiency do not.

s: Vitamin B12 deficiency causes pernicious anaemia. Animals cannot synthesise vitamin B12. Humans must obtain all their vitamin B12 from their diet. The complexing metal ion in Vitamin B12 is
x: Vitamin B12 has a cobalt ion (Co3+) at the centre of its corrin ring. Mg2+ is in chlorophyll, Fe2+ in haemoglobin.

s: Which of the following is a fat soluble vitamin that plays a role in blood clotting, bone metabolism and regulating blood calcium levels?
x: Vitamin K is fat-soluble and needed for clotting and bone metabolism (osteocalcin). C and B are water-soluble; A is for vision.

s: Pernicious anaemia is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin ……
x: Pernicious anaemia is due to vitamin B12 deficiency (lack of intrinsic factor). B2, B6 and B1 are not the cause.

s: Deficiency of ………… causes rickets disease.
x: Rickets is caused by vitamin D deficiency; C causes scurvy, A night blindness, B beri-beri/pellagra.

s: Which mineral element is present in Vitamin B-12?
x: Vitamin B12 (cobalamin) contains cobalt; iron is in haemoglobin, magnesium in chlorophyll.

s: Which one of the following is not a natural source of Vitamin A ?
x:
Book key: milk. Strictly, whole milk does contain preformed vitamin A (retinol) in its fat, while mango, papaya and carrot give only provitamin A (beta-carotene).
Mango, papaya and carrot are rich carotene (provitamin A) sources; milk has comparatively little vitamin A, so the book key is milk.

s: The best source of Vitamin C is :
x: Gooseberry (amla) is the best source of vitamin C; apple and mango have less and milk almost none.

s: Vitamin 'C' help in absorption of which of following elements?
x: Vitamin C reduces dietary iron to the ferrous form and increases its absorption; it does not mainly aid calcium, iodine or sodium.

s: The source of vitamin D is –
x: Sun rays let the skin make vitamin D; lemon and orange give vitamin C and cashew nut has almost no vitamin D.

s:
Given below are two statements, one is labelled as
Assertion (A) and other as
Reason (R).
Assertion (A) : Human body synthesizes all the Vitamins required by it.
Reason (R) : Vitamins are essential for proper growth of the body.
Choose the correct answer from the code given below.
Code :
o: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct
x: A is false: the body makes only a few vitamins (D, some K, niacin), so most must come from food. R is true – vitamins are essential for growth.

s:
Assertion (A) : Vitamins are invigorating elements, whose small amount is required for good health.
Reason (R) : Vitamins helps to keep the body healthy by killing harmful bacteria.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but R is not the correct
x: Vitamins are organic compounds needed in small amounts for health, so A is true. They do not kill bacteria (that is antibodies or antibiotics), so R is false.

s: In human body, vitamin A is stored in –
x: Vitamin A is largely stored in the liver in the human body. Its chemical name is retinol whose deficiency causes night blindness.

s: In human body, Vitamin A is stored in –
x: Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin that is stored in the liver, so the liver is the correct answer.

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
s: The vitamin which can be synthesized under the skin in the presence of the uv light of sun is?
x: Vitamin D (the sunshine vitamin) is made in the skin under the sun's UV light.

src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
s: In which season Vitamin A is required in higher quantities?
x:
Official key: Winter. Strictly no authority gives a season-dependent vitamin A requirement for humans ('No seasonal dependence'); deficiency peaks in the hot pre-harvest season (NERC/Cambridge study on India).
The APPSC 2017 key is winter (option A in the paper as printed in Vijeta previous papers). No nutrition authority gives a season-specific vitamin A requirement: ICMR-NIN RDAs depend on age and life stage only.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The Haber process is an industrial method used to produce ammonia by reacting nitrogen and hydrogen gases under high temperature and pressure in the presence of an iron catalyst.
Statement II: The Contact process is an important industrial method used to manufacture sulphuric acid, which involves the catalytic oxidation of sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide using vanadium pentoxide (V2O5) as a catalyst.

Statement I is false, but statement II is true.

src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
s:
Identify the correct pairs of organic chemical reactions and their mechanisms.

1. Gatterman-Koch Reaction - The formation of cyclopropanes from alkenes using methylene carbene.

2. Friedel-Crafts Acylation Reaction - The conversion of carboxylic acids into esters using acids and alcohols.

3. Etard Reaction - The direct oxidation of an aromatic or heterocyclic bound methyl group with an aldehyde using chromyl chloride.

4. Stephen Reaction - The conversion of nitriles to aldehydes in the presence of hydrochloric acid, using tin chloride.
Select the correct answer from the options given below:
x: Etard reaction oxidises an aromatic methyl group to an aldehyde with chromyl chloride, and Stephen reaction reduces nitriles to aldehydes with SnCl2/HCl, so 3 and 4 are right. Gattermann-Koch is formylation of benzene (CO + HCl), not cyclopropanation, and Friedel-Crafts acylation adds an acyl group to an aromatic ring, not esterification.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: When an alcohol is heated with concentrated sulphuric acid at about 170°C, it undergoes dehydration. What is the major product formed?
x: Heating an alcohol with concentrated H2SO4 at about 170°C removes water (dehydration) and gives an alkene, e.g. ethanol → ethene.

src: TS Senior Assistant & Junior Assistant cum Typist 2021
s: Dry ice is used for packing Covid-19 vaccines for transportation. What is dry ice?
x: Dry ice is solid carbon dioxide (sublimes at -78.5°C), used to keep vaccines cold.

src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
s: What is the process of extracting metals from their ores called?
x: Smelting is extracting a metal from its ore by reduction at high temperature in the fused state; refining purifies the metal and mining removes the ore.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Identify the functional group responsible for the characteristic smell of fruits.
x: Esters (RCOOR') give the characteristic fruity smell of fruits and are used in perfumes and flavouring; aldehydes, ketones and carboxylic acids are not the answer.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s:
C2H5OH + alkaline KMnO4 + Heat → X
X + C2H5OH (acid) → Y
What are the products X and Y, respectively?
x: Alkaline KMnO4 oxidises ethanol to ethanoic (acetic) acid (X); the acid reacts with ethanol in acid medium to form an ester, ethyl acetate (Y).

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: Which of the following reactions does not occur in a blast furnace during the extraction of iron?
x: In the blast furnace, coke burns to CO, limestone decomposes to CaO + CO2 and CO reduces Fe2O3 to iron; decomposition of FeSO4 does not occur there.

src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
s: Which of the following is incorrect about acids?
o: Aqueous solutions of acids are electrolytes
Acids can change the colour of certain acid-base indicators
Acids do not react with active metals
x: Acids do react with active metals (e.g. zinc, iron) to give hydrogen gas, so that statement is incorrect. Aqueous acids conduct electricity, taste sour and change indicator colours.

src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: What is the colour of litmus solution when it is neither acidic or basic?
x: Litmus solution is purple in a neutral solution; it turns red in acid and blue in base.

src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
s:
Which of the following statements is/are correct about chemicals and their popular names?

A. The chemical name of 'Alum' is Potassium aluminium sulphate dodecahydrate.

B. The chemical name of 'Aspirin' is Acetyl salicylic acid.

C. The chemical name of 'Chalk' is Hypochlorus acid.
x: Alum (potash alum) is potassium aluminium sulphate dodecahydrate, KAl(SO4)2·12H2O, and aspirin is acetylsalicylic acid, so A and B are correct; chalk is calcium carbonate (CaCO3), not hypochlorous acid.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
s: Tobacco plant contains the following alkaloid?
x: Nicotine is the alkaloid of the tobacco plant; morphine comes from the opium poppy and reserpine from Rauwolfia, and resin is not an alkaloid. (Off-topic: general science.)

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
s: What happens to the colour of litmus paper when you put a drop of acid on it?
o: Blue Litmus paper turns to red
Red Litmus paper turns to blue
Green Litmus paper turns to red
Red Litmus paper turns to green
x: Acids turn blue litmus red; bases turn red litmus blue. (Moved to 5:1.)

src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
s: What is the role of Barium Nitrate (Ba(NO3)2) in fireworks and fountains?
o: It acts as a fuel for combustion.
It produces a blue color in the flames.
It is an oxidizer that produces a green color in the flames.
It produces a red color in the flames.
x: Barium nitrate is an oxidiser in fireworks that gives a green flame; strontium gives red and copper blue. (Moved to 5:1.)

s:
Which of the following statements are correct ?

a. Melamine polymer is used in the manufacture of unbreakable crockery

b. Enzymes are biocatalysts

c. DNA fingerprinting is used for identification of criminals

d. Tincture of iodine is an antiseptic
x: All four are correct: melamine makes unbreakable crockery, enzymes are biocatalysts, DNA fingerprinting identifies criminals and tincture of iodine is an antiseptic.

src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
s:
Identify the compound described below:
- It is present in crude oil and gasoline.
- It can cause Leukemia, DNA Strand Breaks, Chromosomal damage, Cancer, and harmful effects on bone marrow.
- It is known to be carcinogenic to humans.
x: Benzene, found in crude oil and petrol, is a known human carcinogen causing leukaemia and bone-marrow and chromosome damage.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Which property of ammonia explains why it turns red litmus into blue?
x: Ammonia turns red litmus blue because it is a weak base (NH3 + H2O gives NH4+ and OH-); being a reducing agent, soluble or covalent does not explain the colour change. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
s: Atoms are composed of
x: An atom is a small nucleus (protons and neutrons) surrounded by electrons. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: The smallest ketone has ____ carbon atom/s.
x: The smallest ketone is acetone (propanone, CH3COCH3) with 3 carbon atoms, since the C=O must be bonded to two carbons. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: Which of the following could be the molecular formula of an alcohol?
x: C2H6O is ethanol (C2H5OH), a saturated alcohol CnH2n+2O; C2H4O is acetaldehyde, C3H6O acetone or propanal, and CH2O formaldehyde. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: What substance is added to water to dissolve shellac and create a water-based varnish?
x: Shellac dissolves in water when borax (an alkali) is added, giving a water-based shellac varnish; spirit (alcohol) gives the ordinary spirit varnish, not a water-based one.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
s: Which group of elements generally form coloured compounds?
x: Transition (d-block) metals form coloured compounds because of d-d electron transitions in partly filled d orbitals; alkali-metal and non-metal compounds are mostly colourless.

src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
s: Which of the following methods is suitable for preventing cast iron cookware from rusting?
x: Seasoning (coating with fat or oil and heating) forms a protective layer that keeps cast iron from rusting; soap and abrasives strip that layer.

src: APPSC Royalty Inspector, Agriculture Officers, Town Planning
s: Which of the following is an emulsion?
x: Butter is an emulsion (water droplets dispersed in fat); vinegar, sugar solution and honey are solutions.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Sulphur is used in vulcanization. This process is mainly associated with
x: Vulcanisation is heating natural rubber with sulphur, which cross-links it and makes it harder, stronger and more elastic and wear-resistant (tyres, footwear). Steel, glass and cement making do not use it.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: The ignition temperatures of four substances P, Q, R and S are 95°C, 98°C, 105°C and 108°C, respectively. Which substance/s will catch fire when they are exposed to a temperature of 100°C?
x: A substance catches fire only when its temperature reaches its ignition temperature. At 100°C, P (95°C) and Q (98°C) are above their ignition temperatures and burn; R (105°C) and S (108°C) stay below theirs, so only P and Q catch fire.

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
s: Goiter is characterized by:
x: Goitre is the enlargement of the thyroid gland, mostly due to iodine deficiency.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: The axial skeleton consists of the skull, vertebral column, rib cage and sternum, providing structural support and protection to vital organs.
Statement II: The tibia is the longest and strongest bone in the human body, located in the upper arm.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both statement I and statement II are false.
Both statement I and statement II are true.
x: Statement I is true (skull, vertebral column, ribs and sternum form the axial skeleton). Statement II is false: the femur (thigh) is the longest and strongest bone, and the tibia is in the lower leg, not the arm.

src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
s: The Right Hemisphere of the brain handles?
x: The right cerebral hemisphere is dominant for spatial abilities (also face recognition, visual imagery); language is mainly left-hemisphere. Off-topic (psychology).

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which of the following is a diuretic
x: Furosemide (loop diuretic), mannitol (osmotic diuretic) and acetazolamide (carbonic anhydrase inhibitor) all increase urine output, so all of these are diuretics.

src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
s: Which is the most abundant element by mass in human body?
x: Oxygen is the most abundant element by mass in the human body (~65%), followed by carbon and hydrogen. Off-topic (general science), moved.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Commonly used absorbable suture material is
x: Catgut, made from animal intestine (collagen), is the classic absorbable suture. Silk and nylon are non-absorbable, and fascia lata is a tissue graft.

src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
s:
When it comes to the digestive system, which statements are true?

I. The pancreas produces digestive enzymes and insulin.

II. The small intestine is where most nutrient absorption occurs.

III. The gallbladder stores bile produced by the liver.
x: The pancreas makes digestive enzymes and insulin, most absorption is in the small intestine, and the gall bladder stores bile – all three true. Off-topic, moved.

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) & Technical Assistan
s: What is the resting rate heart for a normal person?
x: A normal adult resting heart rate is 60 to 100 beats per minute (American Heart Association); about 72 is the textbook average.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: A process of deposition of calcium and other minerals on the surface of the cartilage is called.
x: Deposition of calcium and other minerals that turns cartilage into bone is ossification. Off-topic (biology), moved.

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Hydrogeology) in AP Ground Water
s: The production of tears when dust particles hit the human eye; is an example of which of the following?
x: Tears flushing dust from the eye are part of the body's first-line (innate) defence – immunity; they contain lysozyme. Off-topic (biology), moved.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: What is a characteristic feature of a first-degree burn?
o: Minor epithelial damage, presence of redness
Partial thickness burn and scalds, may be painful
x: A first-degree (superficial) burn damages only the epidermis, with redness and pain; partial-thickness is second degree and full-thickness/necrosis third degree. Off-topic (first aid), moved.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Which instrument is used to measure blood pressure?
x: Blood pressure is measured with a sphygmomanometer. Off-topic (biology/health), moved.

src: APPSC Technical Assistant (Geo Physics) / Technical Assistan
s: In case of heat stroke, the body temperature?
x: In heat stroke the body's cooling fails and core temperature rises quickly (above 40°C). Off-topic (health), moved.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
s: The weight of a brain of a normal human adult is about
x: An adult human brain weighs about 1.3-1.4 kg, i.e. about 3 pounds.

src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the excretory system in humans?
x: Nissl's granules are in the cell body of a neuron (nervous system), not the excretory system; the glomerulus, Bowman's capsule and Henle's loop are parts of the nephron. Off-topic (human biology), moved to book 5.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: An abnormal cavity containing pus is called as
x: An abscess is a localised cavity filled with pus; a hematoma is collected blood, a cyst a fluid sac, a tumour a mass of cells. Off-topic (health), moved to book 5.

src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
s: Tooth enamel is made up of which of the following?
x: Tooth enamel, the hardest substance in the body, is made of calcium phosphate (hydroxyapatite). Off-topic (biology), moved to book 5.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
s:
Which of the following statements is/are NOT correct with respect to definition of anatomy and physiology?

I. Physiology focuses on the physical arrangement of parts in the body.

II. Anatomy studies the inner functioning of cells, tissues and organs.
o: Only statement I is not correct
Only statement II is not correct
Both statements I and II are not correct
Both statements I and II are correct
x: Both statements swap the definitions: anatomy studies the structure (physical arrangement) of body parts, physiology studies how cells, tissues and organs function – so both are not correct.

src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
s: Which of the following is a procedure used to save an abscessed tooth in which the pulp chamber is cleaned out, disinfected, and filled with a permanent filling?
x: Root canal therapy cleans, disinfects and fills the pulp chamber of an abscessed tooth; gum grafts and gingivoplasty treat gums. Off-topic (biology), moved.

src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the human female reproductive system?
x: The vas deferens carries sperm in the MALE reproductive system; fimbriae (of the fallopian tube), cervix and endometrium (uterine lining) are female parts.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: Which of the following is not a part of the female reproductive system in human beings?
x: The vas deferens carries sperm in the male reproductive system; ovary, uterus and fallopian tube are female organs. (Biology; moved.)

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s:
Match Table-I with Table-II and choose correct code.
Table-I - Table-II

A. Lipase -
1. Breaks lactose

B. Amylase -
2. Breaks fat

C. Trypsin -
3. Breaks starch

D. Lactase -
4. Breaks Protein
x: Lipase breaks fat, amylase breaks starch, trypsin breaks protein and lactase breaks lactose: A-2, B-3, C-4, D-1.

src: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers (Main
s: In humans, Milk Teeth generally fall off at what age?
x:
Most books and keys: between 6 and 8 years. Strictly: shedding starts at about 6 and is complete by about 12 (incisors 6-8, canines and molars 9-12) (AAP healthychildren.org; Wikipedia 'Deciduous teeth').
Milk (deciduous) teeth begin to fall at about 6 years, and the incisors are shed by about 6-8 years, so most keys give 6-8. Shedding of canines and molars continues until about 12, which is why 10-12 is only the end of the process.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: The classical example for closed wound is
x: A contusion (bruise) is the classic closed wound, with the skin unbroken; lacerated, penetrating and incised wounds are open.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: One of the following is not administered through rectum
x:
Key: ecbolic (a drug class, usually injected), since suppositories and enemas are by definition rectal preparations. Strictly, one ecbolic (misoprostol) can also be given rectally (Wikipedia, Uterotonic).
Ecbolics (drugs such as oxytocin that stimulate uterine contraction) are given by injection, not per rectum, whereas suppositories and enemas are rectal preparations. (Off-topic: moved to general science.)

src: APPSC Teaching Staff of the Department of Technical Educatio
s: In a healthy adult, what is the approximate percentage of white blood cells in total blood volume?
x: White blood cells (with platelets) form well under 1% of blood volume (the thin buffy coat), so 'one percent' is the nearest figure.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: The tube that connects the pharynx with the stomach is the
x: The oesophagus (food pipe) connects the pharynx to the stomach; the duodenum and jejunum are parts of the small intestine and the pylorus is the stomach's outlet.

src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2
s: Which cranial nerve in humans is the largest and has both, sensory and motor functions?
x: The trigeminal (5th) nerve is the largest cranial nerve and has both sensory and motor fibres.

src: APPSC Asst. Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains Paper
s: It is always better to eat/drink the following foods in case of heat stroke?
x: Fluids such as lemon water or buttermilk restore water and salts in heat stroke; proteins, meat and dry fruits add heat load.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which of the following is not a solid form of medicine
x: Syrup is a liquid dosage form; tablets, capsules and boluses are solid.

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
s: Calcium along with which mineral is required for the strength of skeletal muscle?
x: Calcium phosphate gives bones (the skeleton that muscles pull on) their strength, so phosphorus goes with calcium; the stem's 'skeletal muscle' means the skeletal system.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: The gaseous exchange in humans takes place in
x: Gas exchange in the lungs takes place in the alveoli, across their thin walls into the capillaries. Off-topic (biology), moved.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
s: The longest fibre on the cell body of a neuron is called:
x: The axon is the single long fibre that carries impulses away from the neuron's cell body; dendrites are short and branched.

s: What is the immediate first aid that can be administered to a victim of burns?
o: Wetting the burnt part in cold water
Removing stuck cloth on the burnt part
x: Immediate first aid for a burn is to cool the part in cool or cold running water. Stuck cloth must not be pulled off, butter or ointment should not be applied, and water should not be poured with force.

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the human respiratory system?
x: Schwann cells form the myelin sheath of peripheral nerves (nervous system); trachea, bronchi and larynx are parts of the respiratory tract.

src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
s: Number of Incisors, Canines, Premolars and Molars in humans is respectively
x: Human adult dentition (32 teeth) = 8 incisors, 4 canines, 8 premolars, 12 molars (dental formula 2123 per half-jaw).

src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
s: The visual acuity of 20/200 is characteristic feature of
x: Visual acuity of 20/200 (seeing at 20 feet what a normal eye sees at 200 feet) in the better eye with correction is the usual threshold of legal blindness.

s: Which of the following are parts of the excretory system?
x: Bowman's capsule and Henle's loop are parts of the nephron in the kidney; colon, rectum, appendix and ileum belong to the digestive system.

src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
s: Which of following is NOT a part of the human excretory system?
x: Alveoli are air sacs of the lungs (respiratory system); nephrons, Bowman's capsule and ureters belong to the excretory system.

src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
s: Which of the following is a voluntary muscle that you can control consciously?
x: Skeletal (striated) muscle is voluntary; smooth and cardiac muscles are involuntary.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: The capsules that contain medicines taken by us are normally made of
x: Medicine capsule shells are normally made of gelatin (from collagen), which dissolves in the stomach.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which of the following is used to control Mange
x: Sulphur ointment (sulphur, often with lime) is the classic remedy for mange, a mite infestation of animal skin.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
s: What is range of the pH value of the human blood?
x: Human blood is slightly alkaline, pH 7.35-7.45.

src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
s: Which of the following assist the eye lens to adjust its focus for viewing bodies at different distances?
x: The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens (accommodation) to focus near and far objects. The pupil only controls light entry; rods and cones are retinal receptors.

src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
s: Hyper Natrimia is excess presence in blood of?
x: Hypernatraemia means too much sodium in the blood (natrium = sodium).

src: APPSC Assistant Motor Vehicle Inspector General Studies & Me
s: Which of the following are the main constituents of Dettol, a commonly used antiseptic in homes?
x: Dettol's main constituents are chloroxylenol and alpha-terpineol (with pine oil); it has no iodine.

src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
s: The gap between two neurons is called a
x: The junction between two neurons is a synapse; dendrites and axons are parts of a neuron, and an impulse is the signal it carries.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: What is the average lung capacity of an adult human being (choose nearest figure)?
x: Total lung capacity of an adult is about 6 litres (vital capacity ~4.5–4.8 L).

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: For the examination of skin scrapings which of the following is required
x: Skin scrapings are cleared with 10-20% potassium hydroxide (KOH mount) so that fungal elements and mites can be seen. Heparin is an anticoagulant, and HCl and dichromate are not used for this.

src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: If a person closes one eye and looks with the other eye only, he would see?
x: With one eye we lose binocular depth perception, so the world looks flat, i.e. two-dimensional (the usual key). Colour vision is not lost.

src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
s: What is the primary function of the human digestive system?
o: To break down food and absorb nutrients
To provide Oxygen to the body
x: The digestive system breaks food down into simple absorbable molecules and absorbs the nutrients; temperature control, blood circulation and oxygen supply belong to other systems.

src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
s: How many valves are present in a human heart?
x: The human heart has four valves: tricuspid, pulmonary, mitral (bicuspid) and aortic. (Off-topic: human biology.)

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
s: Which blood vessels have the smallest diameter?
x: Capillaries are the narrowest blood vessels (about 5–10 micrometres), one cell thick. (Off-topic: biology.)

src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
s: Which of the elements found in human body has functional requirement?
x:
Official key: Arsenic. Strictly: arsenic's essentiality in humans is unproven (it is a toxic element); none of the options is an established essential element.
Among the options only arsenic is treated as a (possibly essential) ultra-trace element with a functional role; titanium, caesium and aluminium have no known requirement.

src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
s: Which part of the eye gives it a distinctive colour?
x: The iris is the pigmented muscular ring around the pupil and gives the eye its colour. The cornea is transparent, the pupil is an opening and the retina lies at the back.

src: APPSC Assistant Conservator of Forest (General Studies & Men
s: The human saliva has an average pH of____.
x: Human saliva is slightly acidic to near-neutral, pH about 6.2-7.6 with an average of about 6.7 (salivary amylase works best near this); 5.5 is the enamel-dissolving critical pH, and 7.8 and 9.1 are too alkaline.

src: APPSC Assistant Engineers General Studies & Mental Ability 2
s: Which enzyme helps in the digestion of fats in the gut of humans?
x: Lipase digests fats (pancreas, intestine); amylase digests starch, lactase lactose, and helicase unwinds DNA.

src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
s: Which of the following enzymes found in saliva is responsible for digestion?
x: Saliva contains salivary amylase (ptyalin), which digests starch; pepsin acts in the stomach, trypsin from the pancreas.

src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St
s: Of the following bacteria, ____ causes pneumonia.
x: Haemophilus influenzae causes pneumonia (as does Streptococcus pneumoniae); S. thermophilus and Lactobacillus are curd/yoghurt bacteria and E. coli is a gut bacterium.

src: APPSC AE (Environmental) Mains General Studies & Mental Abil
s: Which enzyme is found in tears?
x: Tears contain lysozyme, an antibacterial enzyme that breaks down bacterial cell walls. Ptyalin is in saliva, pepsin in the stomach, and sebum is skin oil. (Off-topic: human physiology.)

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Which body fluid plays an important role in transporting digested fats in humans?
x: Digested fats are absorbed into the lacteals (lymph vessels) of the villi and carried by lymph, not directly by blood.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: What is the main function of the kidneys in the human body?
o: To filter waste products and excess of water from the blood
Help the body to absorb nutrients from the food
To pump the blood throughout the body
x: The kidneys filter waste products and excess water from the blood and form urine; digestion, absorption and pumping are other organs' jobs.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
s: Which of the following is the longest part of the alimentary canal?
x: The small intestine (about 6-7 m) is the longest part of the alimentary canal.

src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: Fat in the food eaten by us is completely digested in?
x: Fats are completely digested in the small intestine by bile (emulsification) and pancreatic and intestinal lipase.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s: The digestive fluid bile is produced by which organ of the human body?
x: Bile is produced by the liver and only stored in the gall bladder.

src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
s: The duodenum is a part of the
x: The duodenum is the first part of the small intestine.

src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper (General Studie
s: Nerves of the brain responsible for sending and receiving information
x: Neurons (nerve cells) send and receive information in the brain and nerves.

src: APPSC Assistant Director in AP Economic & Statistics General
s: If all the alveoli in a human lung are separated and spread, they will occupy the size of a typical?
x: The roughly 300-500 million alveoli have a surface area of about 70 m² – about a tennis court.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: Identify the gland, which release HCl in human digestive tract.
x: Gastric glands of the stomach wall release HCl.

src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S1) General Studies & Mental Ab
s: Leucocytes are also known as ____ as they are colourless due to the lack of haemoglobin.
x: Leucocytes are white blood cells – colourless because they lack haemoglobin.

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s: The ____ in the iris that make pigment are called melanocytes.
x: Melanocytes are the cells that make melanin pigment in the iris.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
s: Red blood cells are formed in
x: Red blood cells are formed in the red bone marrow.

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
s: Which drugs are used to lower the body temperature?
x: Antipyretics (e.g. paracetamol) lower raised body temperature; analgesics relieve pain.

src: APPSC ASO Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: Which of the following carries Carbon dioxide rich blood from heart to lungs in humans?
x: The pulmonary artery carries deoxygenated (CO2-rich) blood from the right ventricle to the lungs; pulmonary veins return oxygenated blood.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: The largest artery in the human body
x: The aorta, leaving the left ventricle, is the largest artery of the body.

src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
s: A blood vessel which pumps the blood from the heart to the entire body
x: Arteries carry blood from the heart to the body (the aorta from the left ventricle); veins return it and capillaries exchange materials.

src: APPSC Sample Taker General Studies & Mental Abilities 2023
s:
Match the given organs with the arteries which supply blood to them.
Organ:

I. Kidney

II. Liver

III. Heart
Arteries which supply blood:

a. Renal arteries

b. Hepatic arteries

c. Coronary arteries
x: Renal arteries supply the kidney, hepatic arteries the liver and coronary arteries the heart: I-a, II-b, III-c.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
s: Alimentary canal runs from mouth to?
x: The alimentary canal is the continuous tube from the mouth to the anus (mouth, oesophagus, stomach, small and large intestine, rectum, anus).

src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in A.P Sainik Welfare Sub Service Ge
s: Which of the following systems of the human body is responsible when a person sneezes?
x: Sneezing is a reflex of the respiratory system: irritants in the nasal lining trigger a forceful expulsion of air through the nose and mouth. It is controlled by the medulla, but the system involved is respiratory, not immune (printed key: immune system).

s: Anorexia and bulimia are types of ____ disorders.
x: Anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa are eating disorders (self-starvation; binge eating with purging).

src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I (Mains) General Studies & Mental Abil
s: A cardiac portion, a fundic region and a pyloric portion are parts of which of the following organs/body parts?
x: The stomach has a cardiac part (near the oesophagus), a fundic region and a pyloric part (opening into the duodenum).

src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer & Other Posts General St

2. Leukocytes
3. Thrombocytes

src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
s: Anorexia nervosa is a ....disorder.
x: Anorexia nervosa is an eating disorder (self-starvation from fear of weight gain).

s: Which of the following is NOT a region of the human stomach?
x: Serosa is the outermost layer of the wall of the alimentary canal, not a region of the stomach. The stomach's regions are the cardiac part (where the oesophagus opens), the fundus, the body and the pyloric part (which opens into the duodenum).

s: All of the following are tests for brain, spinal cord, and nerve disorders, EXCEPT ______
x: Bronchoscopy examines the airways and lungs, not the nervous system. Myelography (spinal cord imaging), electroencephalography (EEG – brain's electrical activity) and echoencephalography (ultrasound of the brain) are nervous-system tests.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: The part of the brain that controls involuntary actions such as blood pressure, salivation and vomiting
x: The medulla oblongata controls involuntary actions – heartbeat, blood pressure, breathing, salivation, swallowing and vomiting. The cerebrum handles voluntary action and thought, the cerebellum balance, and the diencephalon (hypothalamus) temperature, hunger and thirst.

src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
s: Which part of the brain controls the process of Breathing?
x: Breathing is controlled by the respiratory centre in the medulla oblongata (with the pons). The cerebellum controls balance, the hypothalamus temperature/hunger, the cerebrum voluntary actions.

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: Which of the following represents the gap between two neurons?
x: A synapse is the junction (gap) between two neurons across which the impulse passes, usually by neurotransmitters. The dendrite receives and the axon carries the impulse; the impulse is the signal itself, not a gap. (Biology PYQ: moved to book 5 row 1.)

s: Suppose you have four test tubes labelled as ‘A’, ‘B’, ‘C’ and ‘D’. ‘A’ contains plain water, ‘B’ contains solution of an alkali, ‘C’ contains solution of an acid, and ‘D’ contains solution of sodium chloride. Which one of these solutions will turn phenolphthalein solution pink?
x: Phenolphthalein turns pink in basic (alkaline) solution. Tube B has an alkali, while water, acid and NaCl solution are neutral or acidic and leave it colourless.

s: Which of the following metals is the most reactive metal?
x: In the reactivity series calcium lies far above zinc, iron and copper, so it is the most reactive of these.

s: Zinc is used to protect iron form corrosion because zinc is
o: a good conductor of heat and electricity.
x: Zinc is more electropositive (more reactive) than iron, so it corrodes in preference to iron and protects it (galvanisation, sacrificial protection).

s: Which one of the following gives the highest amount of hydrogen ions (H+)?
x: Gastric juice contains HCl (pH ~1.5-3.5), so it is the most acidic and has the highest H+ concentration; lemon juice is a weaker acid and the others are basic.

s: Which of the following acids is present in ant bites?
x: Ant bites inject formic acid (methanoic acid), as the notes state.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Chemical used for preserving the serum is
x: Merthiolate (thiomersal), a mercury compound, is the classic preservative for serum and vaccines. Heparin and oxalates are anticoagulants that stop blood clotting, and formaldehyde is a tissue fixative, not a serum preservative.

s: What is Bisphenol A (BPA)?
o: A medical test for detecting cancer
A test for testing the use of drugs to improve performance by athletes
A chemical used for the development of food-packaging materials
A special type of alloy steel
x: Bisphenol A is an industrial chemical used to make polycarbonate plastics and epoxy food-can linings, i.e. food-packaging materials. It is not a medical test, a doping test or an alloy steel.

s: What is Bisphenol A (BPA)?
o: A medical test for detecting cancer
A test for testing the use of drugs to improve
A chemical used for the development of food-
A special type of alloy steel
x: BPA is used in polycarbonate plastics and food-can linings, so it is a chemical used for food-packaging materials. The other options (medical test, doping test, alloy steel) do not describe it.

s: Gold is dissolved in –
o: Mixture of Sulfuric and Nitric Acid
Mixture of hydrochloric acid and nitric acid (aqua regia)
x:
The printed options did not include the correct answer (Mixture of hydrochloric acid and nitric acid (aqua regia)); it is added as option 5.
Gold dissolves only in aqua regia, a 3:1 mixture of concentrated hydrochloric and nitric acids. No single acid dissolves it, and a sulphuric–nitric mixture does not either, so the printed key (c) is wrong.

s: Mustard gas is used –
o: As a source of mustard oil
x: Mustard gas (sulphur mustard) is a blistering chemical-warfare agent. It has nothing to do with mustard oil, fuels or deodorants.

s: During the first world war, which of the following gas was utilised as the chemical weapon?
x: Mustard gas (sulphur mustard) was used as a chemical weapon in World War I, along with chlorine and phosgene. Carbon monoxide and hydrogen cyanide were not the typical battlefield agents.

s: What is the chemical name of the deadly poison ‘cyanide’?
x: Prussic acid is hydrocyanic acid (HCN), whose salts are the cyanides. Sulphuric, hydrochloric and nitric acids are mineral acids, not cyanide.

src: APPSC AEE Mains General Studies & Mental Ability 2016
s: Stinging hair of nettle leaves inject the following acid causing burning pain?
x: Nettle leaf hairs inject formic (methanoic) acid, causing the burning pain. Acetic acid is vinegar, phosphoric acid is in colas and sulphuric acid is a mineral acid.

src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
s: Which of the following materials in normally used in a breath analyzer test to ascertain whether a person is drunk or not?
x: In the breath analyser, orange acidified potassium dichromate turns green as it oxidises the alcohol in the breath. Permanganate, silica gel and baking soda are not used.

src: APPSC Assistant BC Welfare Officer and Royalty Inspector in
s: What is the dominant acid in a 'bee sting'?
x: School books and Rocket list formic (methanoic) acid as the acid of a bee sting. Lactic, malic and citric acids come from muscles, apples and lemons.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: Hard coffee stains on clothes can be properly removed by?
x: Sodium hypochlorite (bleach) is an oxidising agent that breaks down the coloured compounds of tea and coffee stains on white cloth. Water and lemon juice only lighten fresh stains, and petrol removes grease, not coffee.

s: Cola type soft drinks contain:
x: Cola drinks are acidified with phosphoric acid, which gives their tangy taste. Formic, lactic and acetic acids are not cola ingredients.

s:
Consider the following statements
1.
Assertion (A): Formic acid is a stronger acid than acetic acid.
2.
Reason (R): Formic acid is an organic acid.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
o: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
x: Formic acid is stronger than acetic acid because acetic acid's CH3 group pushes electrons and weakens it. Formic acid is also an organic acid, but that does not explain why it is stronger, so both are true and R is not the explanation.

s: When ants bite, they inject:
x: Ants inject formic acid (from Latin formica, ant), which causes the burning sensation. Acetic acid, methanol and stearic acid are not involved.

s: Chlorination is a process used for water purification. The disinfecting action of chlorine is mainly due to:
o: The formation of hydrochloric acid when chlorine is added to water
The formation of hypochlorous acid when chlorine is added to water
The formation of nascent oxygen when chlorine is added to water
The formation of hydrogen when chlorine is added to water
x: Chlorine reacts with water to form hypochlorous acid (HOCl) and HCl; HOCl is the strong disinfectant that kills microbes. HCl does not disinfect, and 'nascent oxygen' is an older textbook explanation.

s: Which is the most reactive metal ?
x: Potassium is at the top of the reactivity series (K > Na > Ca > Fe), so it is the most reactive of the four metals.

s: Soft drinks such as colas contain significant quantities of :
x: Colas contain significant caffeine, a stimulant alkaloid. Nicotine is in tobacco, tannin in tea and renin is a kidney enzyme.

s: Which acid is mainly find in lemons?
x: Lemon contains citric acid. Acetic acid is in vinegar, ascorbic acid is vitamin C and nitric acid is a mineral acid.

s: When ants bite, they inject :
x: Ants inject formic acid, a simple carboxylic acid. Glacial acetic acid, methanol and stearic acid are wrong.

s: What is the dominant chemical present in vinegar?
x: Vinegar is dilute acetic acid, whose IUPAC name is ethanoic acid. Formic acid is the ant-sting acid and malic acid is in apples.

s: Food cans are coated with tin but not with zinc because
o: zinc has a higher melting point than tin.
zinc is more reactive than tin.
tin is more reactive than zinc.
x: Zinc is more reactive than tin, so it would react with food acids and form harmful salts; tin is less reactive and safe. Cost and melting point are not the reason.

s: Citric acid is present in free form in
x: Lemon contains citric acid in free form. Tamarind mainly has tartaric acid, apple malic acid and milk lactic acid.

s: Sodawater obtained by passing carbon dioxide in water is
x: CO2 dissolves in water to form carbonic acid, so soda water is acidic. It is not basic, and it is neither an oxidising nor a reducing agent.

s: Which one of the following acids is used in the manufacturing of baking powder ?
x: Baking powder is baking soda plus a mild edible acid, tartaric acid. Oxalic acid is toxic, and lactic and benzoic acids are not its acid component.

s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Caffeine, a constituent of tea and coffee is a diuretic.
2. Citric acid is used in soft drinks.
3. Ascorbic acid is essential for the formation of bones and teeth.
4. Citric acid is a good substitution for ascorbic acid in our nutrition.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
x: Caffeine is a diuretic, citric acid is used in soft drinks and ascorbic acid (vitamin C) is needed for collagen in bones and teeth. Citric acid cannot replace ascorbic acid, so 1, 2 and 3 only.

s: Which one of the following does not contain COOH group?
x: Ascorbic acid is acidic because of an enol hydroxyl in a lactone ring and has no carboxyl group. Citric, lactic and tartaric acids are all carboxylic (–COOH) acids.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional

o: Could be an acid or base
x: Bases turn red litmus blue; acids turn blue litmus red, and a neutral salt changes neither.

s: If Hydrochloric Acid is added to few pieces of Zinc in a beaker and a burning match stick is brought near the mouth of the beaker, then?
o: The gas inside the beaker catches fire
The match stick burns at original intensity
The match stick burns at reduced intensity
x: Zinc and dilute HCl give hydrogen gas, which catches fire with a pop when a burning match is brought near. The match is not put out, because hydrogen is combustible.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: During winter in cold regions, bottles of vinegar are found to freeze. This happens because
o: Pure ethanoic acid has a high melting point
Pure ethanoic acid has a low melting point
Pure ethanoic acid is a strong acid
Pure ethanoic acid is a weak acid
x: Pure (glacial) ethanoic acid melts at about 290 K (16.6 °C), well above winter temperatures in cold regions, so it freezes; that is why it is called glacial acetic acid (NCERT). A low melting point would keep it liquid, so the printed key 'low melting point' is wrong.

s: A man posing as goldsmith went to a house and informed the lady of the house that he will polish her gold ornaments for a nominal amount. He dipped the ornaments given by her in a solution called royal water and they sparkled like new. After he left, the lady weighed the ornaments and found that they reduced in weight. What could be the solution?
x: 'Royal water' is aqua regia (3 HCl : 1 HNO3), the only common reagent that dissolves gold, so the ornaments lost weight. Oil of vitriol is H2SO4 and aqua fortis is HNO3; neither dissolves gold alone.

s: Bleaching action of chlorine is due to which reaction?
x: Chlorine bleaches by oxidation: with water it forms hypochlorous acid, which gives nascent oxygen that oxidises the coloured matter.

s: ‘Oil of Vitriol’ is the common name of which of the following?
x: Oil of vitriol is concentrated sulphuric acid (H2SO4), the 'king of chemicals'. Blue vitriol is copper sulphate.

s: Which one of the following is an organic acid?
x: Acetic acid (vinegar) is an organic (carboxylic) acid. HCl, HNO3 and H2SO4 are mineral acids.

s:
Which among the following is an incorrect pair? (Natural Source – Acid)

I. Vinegar – Acetic acid

II. Curd – Lactic acid

III. Tamarind – Citric acid
Codes
x: Tamarind's acid is tartaric acid, not citric acid, so only pair III is incorrect. Vinegar is acetic acid and curd is lactic acid.

s: Which one of the following was the first mineral acid discovered?
x:
Most keys (Testbook, NDA 2020): sulphuric acid. Some solution books: nitric acid. The history is not settled; the alchemists knew both early.
Sulphuric acid ('oil of vitriol') is usually given as the first mineral acid, known to the medieval alchemists. Some keys give nitric acid instead.

s: Which metal is generally used for coating of brass utensils to prevent copper contamination?
x: Brass and copper vessels are tinned ('kalai') so that food acids do not dissolve copper. Zinc and lead would themselves be toxic, and aluminium is not used for this.

s: Which acid is used in photography–
x: Oxalic acid (as ferrous oxalate developer and in toning) is the acid used in photography. Formic acid is in ant stings, citric acid in lemons and acetic acid in vinegar.

s: Which gas is used in the purification of drinking water?
x: Chlorine is used to disinfect drinking water; it forms hypochlorous acid, which kills germs.

s: Which one of the following organic acids is abundant in grapes, tamarind and banana?
x: Tartaric acid is abundant in grapes, tamarind and banana. Citric acid is in citrus fruits, and lactic acid in curd.

x: Caffeine is the alkaloid of both tea and coffee (also colas). Lemon water has citric acid, not caffeine.

s: Which one among the following metals is more reactive than hydrogen?
x: Tin lies above hydrogen in the reactivity series (Pb, Sn above H), so it displaces hydrogen from dilute acids. Mercury, copper and silver lie below hydrogen.

s: Which one of the following represents the correct order of electron releasing tendency of metals?
x: Zinc is above copper and copper above silver in the reactivity series, so electron-releasing tendency is Zn > Cu > Ag.

s: Which of the following acid found in Apple?
x: Apples contain malic acid; nitric and sulphuric acids are strong mineral acids not found in fruits, and formic acid is found in ant stings.

s: ……… is the primary acid present in ripe bananas.
x: Ripe bananas contain malic acid as their main organic acid; formic acid occurs in ants and the others are mineral acids.

s: Acid turns blue litmus red and base turns red litmus blue. A student tested a liquid with a red litmus paper which remained red with no change. This shows that the liquid
o: is neither an acid nor a base.
must be pure water or acid.
x: Red litmus turns blue only with a base. No change means the liquid is not a base, but it could be an acid or neutral, so only option 1 must be true.

s: When we cut an onion, the synthase enzyme converts the amino acid sulfoxide of the onion into which acid?
x: Cutting an onion releases alliinase (synthase), which converts amino acid sulfoxides into sulfenic acids; these form the tear-inducing compound.

s: The pH of milk is 6. When it turns sour, the pH
x: Souring forms lactic acid by bacterial fermentation, so the acidity rises and the pH falls below 6.

s: Which one of the following elements will not react with dilute HCl to produce H2?
x: Mercury lies below hydrogen in the reactivity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute HCl. Al, Mg and Fe lie above hydrogen and release H2.

s: Which one among the following is the correct order of reactivity of the elements?
x: In the reactivity series the order is Na > Mg > Zn > Cu, with sodium most reactive and copper least.

x: Kwashiorkor results from protein deficiency in a diet that may have enough calories. Vitamin, carbohydrate or water deficiency do not cause it.

s: Which one of the following are the building blocks of proteins?
x: Amino acids are the building blocks of proteins. Ribosomes make proteins, glucose builds carbohydrates and fatty acids build fats.

src: APPSC 2021 Medical Officer (Ayurveda) In Ayush Department
