src: APPSC 2018 Question Papers and Keys for Mains Exams
s: Edema is a typical clinical feature of which disease?
x: Kwashiorkor (protein deficiency) typically shows oedema (swelling). Marasmus is wasting without oedema, and hypertension and fever do not feature oedema as a typical sign.

s: Which one of the following is not a protein ?
x: Oxytocin is a small peptide hormone of nine amino acids, not a protein. Keratin (hair, nails), fibroin (silk) and collagen (connective tissue) are true fibrous proteins.

s: Which one of the following is the richest source of protein?
x: Groundnut has about 25 g protein per 100 g, far more than rice (~7 g) or apple (<1 g).

s: Hair is composed of protein called –
x: Hair is made of the fibrous protein keratin. Casein is milk protein, globulin a blood protein and mucin the protein of mucus.

s: Which one of the following food materials contains all essential amino acids?
x: Egg protein has the highest biological value and contains all essential amino acids in the right proportion, so it is the reference protein. Milk and soybean are good but are not the exam answer; rice lacks lysine.

s: Kwashiorkor, a form of malnutrition, is caused by deficiency of which of the following?
x: Kwashiorkor is protein deficiency with adequate calories (oedema, swollen belly). Selenium, chromium and carbohydrate lack do not cause it.

s: Silk fibre, hairs, nails and claw are made of –
x:
Most books and keys: keratin. Strictly, silk fibre is fibroin, not keratin; only hair, nails and claws are keratin (PMF General Science Part 7, animal fibres: keratin or fibroin).
Hair, nails and claws are made of keratin, the answer books and keys give. Strictly silk is fibroin (another fibrous protein), so keratin is the best of the four; fibrin is the clot protein, elastin and collagen are connective-tissue proteins.

s:
Assertion (A) : Human diet should compulsorily contain glycine, serine and tyrosin.
Reason (R) : Essential amino acids can not be synthesized in the human body.
o: Both (A) and (R) are true, and (R) is the correct
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct
x: Glycine, serine and tyrosine are non-essential – the body makes them – so A is false. R is true: essential amino acids cannot be synthesised and must come from food.

s: Alpha-keratin is a protein, present in :
x: Alpha-keratin is the fibrous protein of the skin's outer layer, hair and nails. Blood and lymph carry albumin and globulins; eggs carry albumin.

s: The disease caused by deficiency of protein in children is–
x: Marasmus is protein-energy malnutrition of infants (severe wasting). Pellagra (B3), beri-beri (B1) and rickets (D) are vitamin deficiencies.

s: The substance responsible for bread-making quality in wheat is –
x: Gluten, the protein of wheat, makes dough elastic and lets bread rise. Globulin is another protein class; glycine and lysine are amino acids.

s: Which one of the following proteins is present in human hair and nails?
x: Keratin forms hair and nails. Oxytocin and vasopressin are peptide hormones; trypsin is a digestive enzyme.

s: Casein is milk :
x: Casein is the main protein of milk (~80% of milk protein); milk sugar is lactose.

s: Which compound present in D.N.A. does not form amino acid ?
x: Adenine, guanine and cytosine are nitrogen bases of DNA; tyrosine is an amino acid, not a DNA component – the odd one out the question intends.

s: Most of the enzymes are :
x: Almost all enzymes are proteins (a few are RNA ribozymes); they are not lipids, acids or alkalis.

s: Which of the following proteins is found in milk ?
x: Casein is the main milk protein. Myosin is muscle protein, haemoglobin blood protein and agglutinins are antibodies.

s: Which one of the following compounds is not stored in human body –
x: Amino acids are not stored – surplus is deaminated and passed as urea. Glycogen (liver, muscle), fat and tocopherol (vitamin E, fat-soluble) are stored.

s: Enzymes are basically –
x: Enzymes are basically proteins (e.g. pepsin, trypsin) acting as biological catalysts; they are not fats, sugars or vitamins.

s: Which of the following disease is caused by severe deficiency of proteins?
x: Kwashiorkor is caused by severe protein deficiency; anaemia (iron), osteoporosis (calcium) and goitre (iodine) are not.

s: Protein requirement of young and old person are –
o: Higher in the young and lower in the old
Higher in the old and lower in the young
Very high in the young and very low in the old
x: Older people need more protein per kg than young adults (about 1.0–1.2 g/kg against 0.8 g/kg) because ageing blunts protein use and causes muscle loss, as the key says.

s: Choose wrong statement regarding proteins :
o: We obtain proteins from both animals and plants
Proteins are made of amino acids
About 30 percent of our body weight comes from
Proteins are called building blocks of our body
x: About 16–20% (NCERT: ~20%) of body weight is protein, not 30%, so (c) is wrong. Proteins come from plants and animals, are made of amino acids and are the body-building nutrients.

s: Tendons through which muscles are connected to bones are tightly compacted bundles of which one of the following long fibrous protein?
x: Tendons are made of collagen, a tough fibrous protein. Fibrin is for clotting, elastin is in elastic tissue and cellulose is not a protein.

s: An enzyme which helps in the digestion of protein is
x:
Most keys: trypsin. Strictly: 'protease' is the class of all protein-digesting enzymes, so it is also true.
Trypsin (pancreas) digests protein; urease breaks urea and sulfatase sulphate esters. 'Protease' is the general class name for all protein-digesting enzymes, not one enzyme.

s: Which one of the following processes in the bodies of living organisms is a digestive process?
o: Breakdown of proteins into amino acids
Breakdown of glucose into CO₂ and H₂O
Conversion of amino acids into proteins
x: Digestion is breaking large food molecules into small absorbable ones, such as proteins into amino acids. The others are respiration or synthesis.

s: Which of the following changes is catalyzed by the enzyme trypsin?
x: Trypsin (pancreatic juice) breaks proteins (and peptones) into smaller peptides; peptidases finish them to amino acids. Pepsin makes peptones.

s: Which one of the following enzymes convert proteins into amino acids?
x: Pepsin is the only protein-digesting enzyme among the options (lactase – lactose, urease – urea, zymase – sugar fermentation); strictly pepsin gives peptides, which other enzymes finish to amino acids.

s:
Assertion (A) : All the proteins in our food are digested in small intestine only.
Reason (R) : The protein-digesting enzyme from the pancreas are released into the small intestine.
Code :

Both (A) and (R) are individually true, but (R) is not
x: Protein digestion starts in the stomach with pepsin, so A is false; R is true – pancreatic trypsin and chymotrypsin enter the small intestine.

s: Which of the following is used in beauty parlours for hair setting?
x: Hair setting and perming work on the sulphur (disulphide) bonds of hair keratin, which are broken and re-formed in the new shape with sulphur compounds (thioglycolates). Chlorine and phosphorus are not used.

s: The plant dye henna imparts orange-red colour to skin and hairs due to its reaction with which of the following?
x: Lawsone, the dye of henna, binds to the proteins (keratin) and amino acids of skin and hair, giving the orange-red stain. It does not react with lipids, carbohydrates or nucleic acids.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M

src: AP High Court Common Test for Multiple Posts 2026
s: Which of the following nutrients is known as the primary 'energy-giving' food for our body?
x: Carbohydrates are the primary energy-giving food. Proteins build the body, and vitamins and minerals regulate it.

s: Which of the following is rich in all the three foods carbohydrates, proteins and fats?
x: Soybean has about 40% protein and 20% fat besides carbohydrate, so it is rich in all three. Rice is mainly carbohydrate, and mango and cabbage are poor in protein and fat.

s: Which of the following is NOT among the essential foods produced by plants each being of value in its own way to human and animal metabolism?
x: Plants make carbohydrates, fats and proteins as essential foods for human and animal metabolism. Nucleic acids (DNA, RNA) are genetic material, not a food group.

s: Which of the following is NOT a macronutrient required for livestock ?
x: Vitamins are micronutrients needed in small amounts, whereas protein, carbohydrates and fats are macronutrients.

s: Which of the following is mostly carbohydrate?
x: Rice has the highest carbohydrate share of the cereals given (~78% of the grain); wheat, barley and maize have more protein and fibre.

s: Which one of the following groups of diet provides maximum energy to human body?
x: Carbohydrate, fat and protein are the energy-giving nutrients (about 4, 9 and 4 kcal/g); vitamins, minerals and water give no energy.

s: The major food fuel during exercise of long duration is
x:
Printed key / most books: carbohydrate. Strictly, in prolonged low- to moderate-intensity exercise fat supplies about half or more of the energy (CSU Nutrition and Fitness 8.6; Nutrition Research Reviews 2003).
The key is carbohydrate: muscle glycogen and blood glucose fuel sustained, high-intensity endurance work, and running out of glycogen ends it. Fat's share rises in very long, gentle exercise, so fat is the tempting option; protein is a minor fuel.

s: Glucose is a source of energy, which one of the following types of molecule is glucose ?
x: Glucose is a monosaccharide – a simple carbohydrate – not a protein, fat or nucleic acid.

s: Which one among the following statements about a healthy diet is correct?
o: Regular eating of high energy snacks between meals is healthy, since it provides energy and vitamins in plenty.
Fruits and vegetables make a good choice because their energy content is high.
A balanced diet must contain plenty of fat and protein with little carbohydrates and fibre.
An optimal quantity of fat, protein carbohydrate with adequate amount of water and fibre makes a healthy diet.

x: Cellulose is a homopolymer of beta-glucose only; proteins and collagen are built from many different amino acids, and agarose has alternating galactose units (agarobiose). (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
s: The most abundant organic compound in world is?
x: Cellulose, the main component of plant cell walls, is the most abundant organic compound on Earth. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
s: The ATP production through respiration is called
x: ATP made in respiration via the electron transport chain is oxidative phosphorylation; photophosphorylation is ATP formation in photosynthesis. (Off-topic; moved to row 1.)

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: In a mammal, what is the ratio of the number of chromosomes in a somatic cell to that in a gamete?
x: Somatic cells are diploid (2n, 46 in humans) and gametes haploid (n, 23), so the ratio is 2:1.

src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon, Group-IV and Other Posts Gene
x: Mitochondria - powerhouse, ATP (3); ribosomes - protein synthesis (1); cell membrane - regulates passage (4); nucleus - control centre with genetic material (2).

s:
Consider the following statements:
1.
Assertion (A): Amoeba is reproduced by fission.
2.
Reason (R): All unicellular organisms are reproduced by asexual methods.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
o: Both (A) and (R) are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both (A) and (R) are individually true and R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
x: Amoeba reproduces by binary fission (A true), but not all unicellular organisms are only asexual - Chlamydomonas, Paramecium (conjugation) and yeast show sexual reproduction (R false).

s:
Arrange the following events of "biogeny theory" in a sequence.

a. Formation of coacervates

b. Aerobic organisms came to existence

c. Heterotropic organisms began to form

d. Mycoplasmas are first formed cells
x: In the biogeny sequence, coacervates formed first, then the first cells (mycoplasma-like), then heterotrophs, and aerobic organisms came last: a, d, c, b. (Off-topic: origin of life.)

s: Recently the State of Tamil Nadu banned the sale of cotton candy due to the presence of which cancercausing agent in it?
x: Rhodamine B, a textile dye, was found colouring cotton candy; it is carcinogenic, so Tamil Nadu banned the sale (Feb 2024). Aristolochic acid comes from some herbal medicines, benzidine is a dye intermediate and 1,3-butadiene a rubber monomer.

s: Which of the following is used as an adulterant of a mustard seed?
x: Argemone (Mexican prickly poppy) seeds look like mustard seeds and are mixed with them; their oil causes epidemic dropsy. Papaya, cumin and coriander seeds are not the usual adulterants of mustard.

s: Which of the following pairs (Fat - Oil) is not correctly matched?
x: Mustard oil is an edible vegetable oil, not a lubricant, so that pair is wrong. Mineral oil comes from petroleum, vegetable fats contain phytosterols and animal fats contain cholesterol.

s: The chemical that is used to ripen mangoes is
x: Calcium carbide reacts with moisture to give acetylene, which acts like the ripening hormone ethylene, so it is (illegally) used to ripen mangoes. Calcium sulphide, carbonate and chloride release no such gas.

s: Improper handling and storage of cereal grains and oilseeds result in the production of toxins known as aflatoxins which are not generally destroyed by normal cooking process. Aflatoxins are produced by
x: Aflatoxins are made by moulds (Aspergillus flavus and A. parasiticus) that grow on badly stored grain and oilseeds. Bacteria, protozoa and viruses do not produce them.

s: Improper handling and storage of cereal grains and oilseeds result in the production of toxins known as aflatoxins, which are not destroyed by the normal cooking process? Aflatoxins are produced by:
x: Aflatoxins are poisonous, cancer-causing chemicals made by moulds such as Aspergillus flavus on stored grain; cooking does not destroy them. Bacteria, protozoa and viruses are wrong.

s: Which of the following chemicals is used for ripening?
x: Calcium carbide gives acetylene, which ripens fruit like ethylene, so it is the chemical used for (artificial) ripening. Sodium and potassium chloride have no ripening action.

src: APPSC Assistant Environmental Engineer and Analyst Grade-II
s: Which of the following is the most common food preservative against mould, bacteria, fungus and yeast?
x: Sorbic acid and its salt potassium sorbate are the commonest preservatives against moulds, yeasts and fungi. Tartaric acid is a food acid, acetylsalicylic acid is aspirin and formic acid only a limited preservative.

s: Sodium benzoate is used as a:
x: Sodium benzoate (E211) is a food preservative that stops bacteria, yeast and moulds in acidic foods and drinks. It is not a flavour, colour or antacid.

s: What causes ‘Blackheart’ in potato ?
x: Blackheart of potato is a storage disorder caused by oxygen deficiency in the tuber's centre. It is not caused by a copper, boron or potassium deficiency.

s: The substance employed for the food processing is
x: Benzoic acid (as sodium benzoate) is a standard food-processing preservative. Sodium carbonate, acetylene and sodium nitrate are not the usual answer.

s: Date of manufacture of food items fried in oil should be checked before buying because oils become rancid due to
x: Fats and oils turn rancid when they are oxidised by air, which is why the manufacture date of fried food matters. Reduction and hydrogenation do not cause rancidity.

s: Fruits stored in a cold chamber exhibit longer storage life because
o: concentration of carbon dioxide in the environment is increased.
there is an increase in humidity.
x: Low temperature slows the respiration rate of fruits, so they ripen and decay more slowly and keep longer. Darkness, CO2 or humidity are not the main reason.

s: What is IQF in food preservations?
x: IQF stands for Individually Quick Frozen, a technique where each piece of food is frozen separately and rapidly to keep texture and quality.

s: Which of the following phytohormone is mainly responsible for fruit ripening ?
x: Ethylene is the gaseous plant hormone that promotes fruit ripening. Cytokinin promotes cell division and abscisic acid is a growth inhibitor.

s: The gas used for artificial ripening of green fruit is
x: Ethylene is the gas (plant hormone) used for artificial ripening of green fruit. Acetylene from calcium carbide only imitates it, and ethane and CO2 do not ripen fruit.

s: Plants contain a variety of sterols like stigmasterol, ergosterol, sitosterol etc which very closely resemble cholesterol. These plant sterols are referred as
x: Plant sterols (stigmasterol, sitosterol, ergosterol) are called phytosterols; ergocalciferol is vitamin D2 and lumisterol a by-product of its synthesis.

s: Artificial chemicals are bio-chemically known as
x: Man-made chemicals that interfere with the hormone system (BPA, phthalates, some pesticides) are called endocrine disruptors. 'Facilitators', 'reactors' and 'inhibitors' are not the accepted term.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
s: Which gas is used to ripen fruits?
x: Ethylene is the gaseous fruit-ripening hormone.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
s:
Which of the following are symptoms of food allergy?

a. Nervousness

b. Fall in blood pressure

c. Atherosclerosis

d. Flushing of the skin

e. Difficulty in swallowing and speaking
x: Food allergy can cause a fall in blood pressure (anaphylaxis), flushing or hives, and swelling of the throat with difficulty in swallowing and speaking. Atherosclerosis is a chronic artery disease, and nervousness is not a typical allergic sign.

s: Which one of the following is the best example of desiccant?
x: Silica gel absorbs moisture and is the standard desiccant (in packets with shoes, medicines, electronics). Polystyrene is a plastic, and NaCl and Na2CO3 are not used as desiccants.

s: Which hormone is found in the gaseous form ?
x: Ethylene is the only plant hormone that is a gas (fruit ripening); abscisic acid, gibberellins and auxins are not gaseous.

s: "Triclosan', considered harmful when exposed to high levels for a long time, is most likely present in which of the following? Environmental Degradation PMF IAS E&E – 44
x: Triclosan is an antibacterial chemical in toiletries such as soaps, toothpaste and deodorants. It is not a food preservative or a ripening agent.

s: 'Triclosan', considered harmful when exposed to high levels for a long time, is most likely present in which of the following?
x: Triclosan is an antibacterial chemical in toiletries such as soaps, toothpaste and deodorants. It is not a food preservative or a ripening agent.

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
s: Sun drying is a method of:
x: Sun drying removes moisture so that microbes cannot grow; it is a traditional method of food preservation (dehydration).

src: APPSC Assistant Statistical Officer Screening Test 2017
s: To store potato chips for a longer period, the sealed packet of chips is normally filled with which gas?
x: Chip packets are flushed with nitrogen, an unreactive gas, so the fats do not get oxidised (rancidity). Off-topic (chemistry), moved.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: What is the freezing temperature used for preserving pork for long period
x: Meat such as pork is stored long-term frozen at about −18°C (0°F) or below; 3–5°C is only chilling. Off-topic (food science), moved.

src: APPSC Dental Assistant Surgeons, Zilla Sainik Welfare Office
s: Most of the artificial food colouring agents are derived from
x: Most synthetic food colours (tartrazine, sunset yellow) are coal-tar (petroleum-derived) dyes. Flowers, fruits and lichens give natural colours.

src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Screeni
s: Why does open portion of a cut apple turn brown when exposed to air?
o: Due to presence of iron in apple
Due to settling of micro dust present in air
As the original inner colour is brown
Due to oxidation of an enzyme present in apple
x: A cut apple browns because its enzyme polyphenol oxidase, exposed to oxygen, oxidises the fruit's phenolic compounds (enzymatic browning); iron, dust or a brown inner colour are not the cause.

src: APPSC Assistant Telugu Translator General Studies & Mental A
s: Retrogradation of starch is the prominent factor bringing about:
x: Retrogradation (re-crystallisation of gelatinised starch) is the main cause of staling of bread.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officers (Grade-II) General Studies & M
s: The ideal temperature for storage of frozen foods is
x: Frozen foods are stored at about -18°C (0°F) or colder, where microbes cannot multiply. The printed '-180°C' is a slip for -18°C; no freezer works at -180°C.

src: APPSC Hostel Welfare Officer Grade-II Screening Test 2017
s: Rancidity is a/an
x: Rancidity is the oxidation of fats and oils, which changes their smell and taste. Antioxidants are added to prevent it.

src: Technical Asst. (Hydrology), Laboratory Assistants in AP Gro
s: Which of the following chemical compound added to bread was banned in India
x: FSSAI removed potassium bromate from the list of permitted additives in 2016 after CSE found it in bread (possible carcinogen). Gluconate, sulphate and oxalate were not the banned bread additive.

s: Natural ripening of climacteric fruits (like apple) occurs due to?
o: Release of ethylene and increased rate of respiration
Release of ethylene and decreased rate of respiration
Release of acetylene and increased rate of respiration
Release of acetylene and decreased rate of respiration
x: Climacteric fruits such as apple ripen through a burst of ethylene release and a sharp rise in respiration (the climacteric rise). Acetylene is used only for artificial ripening, and respiration rises rather than falls.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer General S
s: Development of off odour in fats & oils when they are stored for a longer duration is known as
x: The off-odour and taste that develop in fats and oils on long storage, through oxidation, is called rancidity.

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
s: Primary methods to prevent food spoilage do NOT include:
x: Food spoilage is prevented by refrigeration, drying, salting, canning and preservatives; exposure to air, moisture and microbes causes spoilage, so it is not a method.

src: APPSC Assistant Executive Engineer (AEE) General Studies & M
s:
A statement is given followed by two conclusions.
Select the correct response from the given options.
Statement: Aschelminthes are called roundworms.
Conclusion:
i. The body of the aschelminthes is circular in cross-section.
ii. Roundworms have organ-system level of body organisation.
x:
Printed key: only (i) follows from the statement. Strictly, both (i) and (ii) are true facts (PMF General Science p.89 / NCERT XI: organ-system level), so a fact-check reading gives 'both'.
The name 'roundworm' comes from the body being circular in cross-section, so conclusion (i) follows from the statement. Conclusion (ii) is a true fact (Aschelminthes have organ-system level of organisation) but does not follow from the statement about the name.

src: APPSC Deputy Educational Officer Screening Test (General Stu
s:
Match the following columns I and II and choose the CORRECT answer from the given options.
Column I (Phylum):

A. Ctenophora

B. Porifera

C. Coelenterata (Cnidaria)

D. Echinodermata
Column II (Distinctive features):

1. Choanocytes

2. Bioluminescence

3. Water vascular system

4. Polyp and Medusa
x: Ctenophores show bioluminescence, sponges (Porifera) have choanocytes, Cnidaria have polyp and medusa forms, and echinoderms have a water vascular system: A-2, B-1, C-4, D-3. (Biology, filed under polity by mistake.)

src: APPSC Forest Range Officers Mains General Studies & Mental A
s: Saurology is the
x: Saurology (herpetology of lizards) is the study of lizards.

src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper: Hostel
s: Which of the following features is NOT common in Chordates and non-chordates?
x: Printed key: bilateral symmetry – all chordates are bilaterally symmetrical, but many non-chordates (cnidarians, adult echinoderms) are radial, so it is not common to both groups. Off-topic (zoology), moved.

src: APPSC Group-IV Prelims General Studies & Mental Ability 2022
s: Skull of mammals is
x: Mammals (and amphibians) have a dicondylic skull, joined to the vertebral column by two occipital condyles. Reptiles and birds have a monocondylic skull.

s:
Match the phylum in column A with their features in column B.
Column A (Phylum):

I. Porifera

II. Cnidaria

III. Arthropoda
Column B (Features):

a. Presence of Ostia and Osculum

b. Available in two forms- Polyp and Medusa

c. Have jointed appendages.
x: Porifera – ostia and osculum, Cnidaria – polyp and medusa forms, Arthropoda – jointed appendages. Off-topic, moved.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer (FRO) Paper-I General Studies & M
s:
Which of the following is a correct match of organisms and patterns of organisation of cells in it?
Organism:

I. Sponges

II. Coelenterates

III. Platyhelminthes
Pattern of organisation of cells:

a. Tissue level of organisation

b. Cellular level of organisation

c. Organ level of organisation
x: Sponges – cellular level, coelenterates – tissue level, Platyhelminthes – organ level. Off-topic, moved.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: The beak of an insect eating bird would be?
x: Insect-eating birds have long, sharp/pointed beaks to pick insects (woodpecker, kingfisher-type); short strong beaks crack seeds. Off-topic (biology), moved.

s: Which dog-breed and region-of-origin pair is NOT correctly matched?
x: The Chihuahua comes from Mexico, named after the Mexican state of Chihuahua, not China.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: Which type of snake bite leads to neuroparalytic symptoms?
x: Krait (and cobra) venom is neurotoxic and causes neuroparalysis; Russell's and saw-scaled viper venom is mainly haemotoxic, and pythons are non-venomous.

src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
s: Which one of the following is an animal belonging to the Marsupial category?
x: The koala is a marsupial of Australia that carries its young in a pouch. Rabbit, porcupine and squirrel are placental mammals.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: Respiration in grasshopper takes place through
x: Insects such as the grasshopper breathe through a network of tracheae opening at spiracles; gills and lungs belong to other animals.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s: In which of the following arthropods is the first pair of legs on the cranial segment modified into pincer-like forcipules?
x: Centipedes (Chilopoda) have their first pair of trunk legs modified into poison claws called forcipules. Millipedes have two pairs of legs per segment and no forcipules; cicadas and wasps are insects.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: What is the primary purpose of a Wasp's sting?
o: To defend themselves or their colony
x:
Most books and keys: defence of self and colony. Strictly: in solitary wasps the sting is used mainly to paralyse prey (Britannica, "wasp").
Wasps chiefly use the sting (a modified ovipositor) to defend themselves and the colony. Solitary wasps also use it to paralyse prey, but stinging plays no part in pollination or marking territory.

src: APPSC Junior Assistant cum Typist in Prisons & Correctional
s: Why chameleon changes its colours?
o: To tune its colour with temperature of the day
The colours automatically change on their own
x:
Most books and keys: to protect itself from predators (camouflage). Strictly: chameleons change colour mainly for social signalling and thermoregulation (Stuart-Fox & Moussalli 2008, PLoS Biology).
Most books say chameleons change colour mainly to camouflage themselves against predators. Strictly, colour change serves mainly social signalling and temperature control.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which among the following does not contain crop
x: The emu, a flightless ratite, has no crop. Turkey, duck and quail store food in a crop. (Off-topic: zoology.)

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Sericulture Officer, Ag
s: Which of the following is NOT an example of class Amphibia?
x: Clarias is a catfish (class Pisces), not an amphibian. Bufo (toad), Rana (frog) and Hyla (tree frog) are amphibians. (Off-topic: zoology.)

src: TSLPRB SI Civil Preliminary Written Exam 2018
s:
Match the following:
List-I:
a. Mycology
b. Palynology
c. Oncology
d. Paleontology
List-II: i. study of pollen grains ii. study of treatment of tumours iii. study of fossils of animals and plants iv. study of fungi
x: Mycology is the study of fungi, palynology of pollen, oncology of tumours and palaeontology of fossils, so (a)-(iv), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iii).

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which of the following enzyme is elevated in Downer cow syndrome
x: In downer cow syndrome the recumbent cow suffers muscle damage, so serum creatine phosphokinase (CK) rises sharply; tryptophan and creatinine are not enzymes.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer Screening
s: The foods of Protozoans is digested by
x: Protozoa such as Amoeba digest food with enzymes inside food vacuoles; contractile vacuoles remove water.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: The postmortem sample collected during abortion is
x: After an abortion the aborted fetus (with placenta) is the key post-mortem sample for diagnosing the cause; blood, milk or serum are ante-mortem samples.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: No. of lobes present in left lung of cow
x:
Most keys: 3 lobes (apical/cranial, cardiac/middle, diaphragmatic/caudal). Strictly in current veterinary nomenclature the left lung has 2 lobes, the cranial lobe being split into two parts (general knowledge, not checked).
Classical veterinary anatomy divides the ox's left lung into three lobes (apical, cardiac, diaphragmatic); the right lung has four or five.

s: Mycology is the study of
x: Mycology is the study of fungi; entomology = insects, limnology = fresh waters, volcanology = volcanoes.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Which of the following is not used in lactic acidosis in cattle
x: Rumen lactic acidosis is treated with alkalising agents - sodium bicarbonate, magnesium hydroxide, Ringer's lactate fluids; vinegar (acetic acid) is used for urea/ammonia poisoning, not acidosis.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Pneumatic bones are commonly present in
x: Birds have pneumatic (air-filled) bones that lighten the skeleton for flight; cattle, horses and pigs have solid marrow-filled bones.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: The venom of Russell's Viper primarily affects the
x: Russell's viper venom is haemotoxic: it disrupts blood clotting (consumption coagulopathy, bleeding). Cobra and krait venoms are the neurotoxic ones.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Paste consisting of the drug mixed with either honey/jaggery and administered orally in large animals is called
x: An electuary is a drug mixed into a paste with honey, jaggery or treacle and given by mouth (smeared on the tongue). A bolus is a large pill, a drench a liquid dose, a pessary a vaginal insert.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: The artery used for recording pulse in dog is
x: In dogs the pulse is recorded from the femoral artery on the inner thigh.

src: APPSC Animal Husbandry Department General Studies & Mental A
s: Site of recording pulse in dogs
x: The pulse of a dog is taken at the femoral artery (inner thigh); the coccygeal artery is used in cattle and the jugular is a vein.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: What is the name of the process through which unicellular organisms eat food?
x: Unicellular organisms like Amoeba engulf food by phagocytosis; pinocytosis is the intake of fluid droplets.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer General Studies & Mental Abilit
s:
Read the following statements in respect to difference between 'Poisonous and Venomous animals':

a. If you bite it and you die, it's Poisonous. If it bites and you die, it's Venomous.

b. If you bite it and you die, it's Venomous. If it bites and you die, it's Poisonous.
Which of the above statements is/ are correct?
x: Poisonous animals harm you when you bite or eat them (toxin passively delivered); venomous animals inject venom by biting or stinging. So only statement a is correct.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: Which of the following has a open circulatory system?
x: The cockroach, an insect (arthropod), has an open circulatory system: haemolymph is pumped into open sinuses (haemocoel) and bathes the organs. Fish, snakes and earthworms have closed circulatory systems with blood kept inside vessels.

src: APPSC Forest Subordinate Service (Thanedar) Paper-II General
s: Tracheal respiration occurs in which of the following organisms?
x: Insects such as the cockroach breathe through tracheae: air enters by spiracles and the tracheal tubes take it straight to the tissues. The earthworm breathes through its moist skin, the frog by skin and lungs, and fish by gills.

src: APPSC Forest Beat Officer & Assistant Beat Officer (Mains) P
s: Identify the organisms that undergo cutaneous respiration.
x: Cutaneous respiration (gas exchange through moist skin) is seen in the earthworm and the frog; the frog also uses lungs. Fish breathe by gills and humans by lungs, so every other pair includes a non-cutaneous breather.

src: APPSC Forest Section Officer Screening Test General Studies
s: What is the main function of worker bees in a hive?
x: Worker bees are sterile females that do the colony's work: foraging for nectar and pollen, making honey and wax, nursing the brood and guarding the hive. Only the queen lays eggs, and the drones (males) mate with her, so guarding is only one of the workers' many tasks.

src: APPSC Forest Range Officer Screening Test General Studies &
s:
Consider the following two statements and select the correct option.
Statement I: In a given medium, the speed of sound remains constant regardless of temperature changes.
Statement II: Sound waves are longitudinal waves, meaning the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of wave propagation.
o: Statement I is true, but statement II is false.
Statement I is false, but statement II is true.
Both Statement I and statement II are true.
Both Statement I and statement II are false.
x: Statement I is false – the speed of sound in a medium rises with temperature (about 0.6 m/s per °C in air). Statement II is true: sound waves are longitudinal.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: Which of the following colours would have largest wavelength?
x: In the visible spectrum (VIBGYOR) wavelength rises from violet to red; of orange, yellow, indigo and violet, orange has the longest wavelength.

src: APPSC Endowment Subordinate Service (Mains) Paper-I General
s: A sensitive magnetic field instrument can be effectively shielded from the external magnetic field by placing it inside which of the following materials?
x: Soft iron of high permeability draws the magnetic field lines into itself and so shields the space inside it (magnetic shielding); plastic, wood or a good conductor do not stop a steady magnetic field.

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
s: Rectifiers convert ____.
x: A rectifier converts alternating current (AC) into direct current (DC). (Moved to science in daily life.)

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
s: What happens if you plug in a heater device rated for 110 V, 50 Hz in a household AC electric supply plug in India?
o: It burns out within minutes or even in seconds
Its heat supply would be poorer than its rated value.
You cannot use such a device in an Indian Plug
x: On India's 230 V supply a 110 V heater draws about (230/110)² ≈ 4 times its rated power, so its element burns out quickly. Off-topic (physics).

src: APPSC Draughtsman (Technical Assistant) Paper-I General Stud
s: Under what conditions the resistivity of the material does not change?
o: When the shape of the resistor is changed
When both the material and temperature are changed
x: Resistivity is a property of the material and its temperature, so it does not change when only the shape (length or area) of the resistor changes; resistance would change, resistivity would not.

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
s: Which of the following waves are used for common TV remote control?
x: Common TV remote controls use infrared (IR) light-emitting diodes. Off-topic (physics), moved.

s: Which type of sound waves can propagate in solids?
x: Solids can carry both longitudinal and transverse mechanical waves (like seismic P- and S-waves); fluids carry only longitudinal waves. Off-topic (physics), moved.

src: AP High Court Common Test for Multiple Posts 2026
s: A louder sound is produced by a wave that has a greater
x: Loudness depends on amplitude – a larger amplitude gives a louder sound; frequency decides pitch. Off-topic (physics), moved.

src: APPSC Assistant Chemist (AP Ground Water Service, AP Insuran
s: Which of the following is incorrect about the ultrasonic waves?
o: These waves are can be used for imaging
It cannot be heard by normal human ears
The speed of ultrasonic waves is more in denser media
The ultrasonic waves can travel through vacuum
x: Ultrasonic waves are mechanical sound waves and cannot travel through vacuum; they are inaudible, used for imaging and travel faster in denser media. Moved.

src: APPSC Welfare Organiser in AP Sainik Welfare (General Studie
s: The colour of an opaque object is due to the colour it
x: An opaque object looks the colour of the light it reflects; the other colours are absorbed. Off-topic (physics), moved.

src: APPSC Inspector of Factories, Civil Assistant Surgeons & Fis
s: When a semiconductor is heated, its resistance would
o: Resistance has no relation with temperature
x: A semiconductor has a negative temperature coefficient: heating frees more charge carriers, so its resistance decreases (a metal's would increase). Off-topic (physics), moved.

src: APPSC Zilla Sainik Welfare Officer (Sainik Welfare Service)
s: The electrical resistance of the insulators is
x: An ideal insulator offers (practically) infinitely high resistance to current, hence 'infinitely high' rather than merely 'high'. Off-topic (physics), moved.

src: Previous paper (title page not in scan)
s: The lower limit of the aperture of a pinhole camera is set by?
x: Making a pinhole too small spreads the image by diffraction, which sets its lower limit. Off-topic (physics), moved.

src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
s: What is the cause of dispersion of light through a prism?
x: A prism disperses white light because each colour is refracted by a different amount. Off-topic (physics), moved.

src: APPSC Civil Assistant Surgeon (Specialist) in AP Vaidya Vidh
s: Twinkling of stars is due to?
x: Stars twinkle because of atmospheric refraction by turbulent air layers of changing density. Off-topic (physics), moved.

s: The sun is seen little before it rises and for a short while after it sets. This is because of
o: apparent shift in the direction of sun
x: Atmospheric refraction bends sunlight over the horizon, so the Sun is seen about 2 minutes before sunrise and after sunset. Off-topic (physics), moved.

s:
Consider the following statements

I. The sky appears blue because of scattering.

II. The main cause of seven colors of the rainbow is scattering of light.

III. At the time of sunrise, the sun appears red, due to scattering of light.
Choose the correct statement/s from the given options
x: The blue sky and the red rising Sun are due to scattering (I, III true); the rainbow's colours come from dispersion, not scattering (II false). Off-topic (physics), moved.

s: When the sun is near the horizon during the morning or evening, it appears reddish. The phenomenon that is responsible for this observation is
x: Near the horizon sunlight crosses more air, blue is scattered away and the Sun looks red – scattering. Off-topic (physics), moved.

x: An echo is heard only if the reflected sound arrives at least 0.1 s later; with sound at about 344 m/s the reflector must be at least 344 x 0.1 / 2 = 17.2 m away.

the same as that of men

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017

x: Chicory powder is made from the roasted, ground root of the chicory plant, so the answer is root.

s: The chicory powder which is mixed with coffee is obtained from:
x: Chicory powder used as a coffee additive is made from the roasted roots of the chicory plant, not its stem, leaves or seeds.

src: APPSC Fisheries Development Officer, Assistant Inspector of
s:

b) Proteins

e) Fats
x: Papaya, mango, peaches and apricots are rich in antioxidants (beta-carotene, vitamin C), carbohydrates and soluble fibre; they are poor in protein and fat. So a, c and d.

src: APPSC Assistant Director of Economics, Assistant Commissione
s: The percentage of fat in double toned milk is:
x: Double toned milk has 1.5% fat (and 9% SNF); toned milk has 3% fat.

s: The colour of Cow's milk is slightly yellowish due to the presence of
x: Cow's milk is slightly yellow because of carotene (beta-carotene) in its fat; 'Carolin' is the paper's misprint of carotin (carotene). Riboflavin only gives whey a greenish-yellow tint, so the printed key (b) is wrong.

s: After parboiling, the nutritive value of rice
x: Parboiling drives water-soluble B vitamins and minerals from the husk and bran into the grain, so rice's nutritive value increases.

s: Lutein is a/an:
x: Lutein is a yellow xanthophyll pigment (marigold, egg yolk, the eye's macula). Blue/purple is anthocyanin, orange is carotene.

s: Which of the following accounts for the red colour of tomato?
x: The red colour of tomato is lycopene, a carotenoid. Capsaicin is chilli's pungent compound; carotene is orange and anthocyanin red-purple.

s: An example of modified underground stem is
x: Potato is a stem tuber, a modified underground stem with nodes ('eyes') that bear buds. Carrot and turnip are modified roots, and groundnut is a fruit that develops underground.

s: From which part of pant the ‘Asafoetida or heeng’ is obtained?
x: Asafoetida (heeng) is the dried latex (oleo-gum resin) exuded from the roots of Ferula plants.

src: APPSC Degree Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2017
s: Which is the most widely used method of cooking food?
x: Boiling is the most widely used cooking method in Indian homes (rice, dal, vegetables). Frying, barbecuing and tenderising are less common.

s: Name the scientific instrument to test the purity of milk
x: A lactometer measures the specific gravity of milk and so tests its purity.

s: The percentage of water in milk is measured by
x: A lactometer measures the specific gravity of milk and so its water content. A hygrometer measures humidity, a hydrometer liquid density in general.

s: The density of milk can be obtained by the use of :
x: A lactometer measures the density (specific gravity) of milk. A butyrometer measures fat content.

s: Flower colours of red, pink, blue and purple come mainly from the pigments called ………
x: Anthocyanins are water-soluble pigments that give red, pink, blue and purple colours to flowers. Carotenoids give yellow and orange.

s: Cloves are obtained from
x: Cloves are the dried unopened flower buds of the clove tree (Syzygium aromaticum).

s: ' Oryza sativa ' is the scientific name of:
x: Oryza sativa is cultivated rice. Wheat is Triticum, maize Zea mays and potato Solanum tuberosum.

s: With what is the banana plant propagated?
x: Banana is propagated vegetatively by suckers, the side shoots from the underground stem. Cultivated bananas are seedless, so seeds are not an option.

s: Ginger is a kind of
x: Ginger is a rhizome, an underground stem that stores food, so of these options it is a tuberous stem. It is not a root.

s: The storage organ of which of the following plants is not a stem ?
x: Sweet potato stores food in a tuberous root. Sugarcane, potato and ginger all store food in stems.

s: Tomato belongs to family of:
x: Tomato belongs to Solanaceae, the same family as potato, brinjal and chilli. Gramineae is grasses, Leguminosae is pulses and Malvaceae is cotton and okra.

s: We obtain chilgoza from the seed of species –
x: Chilgoza is the edible seed of the pine Pinus gerardiana.

s: Which of the following underground produced vegetables is a modified root ?
x: Sweet potato is a tuberous (modified) root; potato is a stem tuber, and arbi (bandda) and jimikand (yam) are corms, i.e. stems.

s: In the following pairs of plants and their edible parts, which pair is not correctly matched ?
x: The printed options lost their edible parts; in the original 'Potato – root' is wrong, since the potato is a stem tuber. Ginger (rhizome), onion (bulb) and coconut (endosperm) were correctly matched.

s:
Consider the following features of newer models of motor cars.

I. Radial tyres

II. Streamlined body

III. Multipoint fuel injection

IV. Catalytic converter with exhaust

s:
